verses.translit: Meta tauta eidon, kai idou ohlos polys, on arithmesai auton oudeis edynato, ek pantos ethnoys kai fylon kai laon kai glosson, estotes enopion tou thronoy kai enopion tou arnioy, perivevlimenoys stolas leykas, kai foinikes en tais hersin auton*
verses.translation: After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands;

verses.original: καὶ κράζουσι φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγοντες· Ἡ σωτηρία τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ τῷ θρόνῳ καὶ τῷ ἀρνίῳ.
verses.translit: kai krazoysi fone megale legontes* E sotiria to theo emon to kathimeno epi to throno kai to arnio.
verses.translation: And cried with a loud voice, saying, Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb.

verses.original: καὶ πάντες οἱ ἄγγελοι εἱστήκεισαν κύκλῳ τοῦ θρόνου καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων, καὶ ἔπεσαν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου ἐπὶ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ θεῷ,
verses.translit: kai pantes oi aggeloi eistikeisan kyklo tou thronoy kai ton presvyteron kai ton tessaron zoon, kai epesan enopion tou thronoy epi ta prosopa auton kai prosekynisan to theo,
verses.translation: And all the angels stood round about the throne, and about the elders and the four beasts, and fell before the throne on their faces, and worshipped God,

verses.original: λέγοντες· Ἀμήν· ἡ εὐλογία καὶ ἡ δόξα καὶ ἡ σοφία καὶ ἡ εὐχαριστία καὶ ἡ τιμὴ καὶ ἡ δύναμις καὶ ἡ ἰσχὺς τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· ἀμήν.
verses.translit: legontes* Amin* e eulogia kai e doxa kai e sofia kai e euharistia kai e time kai e dynamis kai e ishus to theo emon eis tous aionas ton aionon* amin.
verses.translation: Saying, Amen: Blessing, and glory, and wisdom, and thanksgiving, and honour, and power, and might, be unto our God for ever and ever. Amen.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀπεκρίθη εἷς ἐκ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων λέγων μοι· Οὗτοι οἱ περιβεβλημένοι τὰς στολὰς τὰς λευκὰς τίνες εἰσὶν καὶ πόθεν ἦλθον;
verses.translit: Kai apekrithi eis ek ton presvyteron legon moi* Outoi oi perivevlimenoi tas stolas tas leykas tines eisin kai pothen elthon;
verses.translation: And one of the elders answered, saying unto me, What are these which are arrayed in white robes? and whence came they?

verses.original: καὶ ⸀εἴρηκα αὐτῷ· Κύριέ μου, σὺ οἶδας. καὶ εἶπέν μοι· Οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ἐρχόμενοι ἐκ τῆς θλίψεως τῆς μεγάλης, καὶ ἔπλυναν τὰς στολὰς αὐτῶν καὶ ἐλεύκαναν ⸀αὐτὰς ἐν τῷ αἵματι τοῦ ἀρνίου.
verses.translit: kai eirika auto* Kyrie moy, su oidas. kai eipen moi* Outoi eisin oi erhomenoi ek tes thlipseos tes megalis, kai eplynan tas stolas auton kai eleykanan autas en to aimati tou arnioy.
verses.translation: And I said unto him, Sir, thou knowest. And he said to me, These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.

verses.original: διὰ τοῦτό εἰσιν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ λατρεύουσιν αὐτῷ ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτὸς ἐν τῷ ναῷ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ ⸂τοῦ θρόνου⸃ σκηνώσει ἐπʼ αὐτούς.
verses.translit: dia touto eisin enopion tou thronoy tou theou, kai latreyoysin auto emeras kai nyktos en to nao autou, kai o kathimenos epi tou thronoy skinosei ep' autoys.
verses.translation: Therefore are they before the throne of God, and serve him day and night in his temple: and he that sitteth on the throne shall dwell among them.

verses.original: οὐ πεινάσουσιν ἔτι ⸀οὐδὲ διψήσουσιν ἔτι, οὐδὲ μὴ πέσῃ ἐπʼ αὐτοὺς ὁ ἥλιος οὐδὲ πᾶν καῦμα,
verses.translit: ou peinasoysin eti oude dipsisoysin eti, oude me pese ep' autous o elios oude pan kauma,
verses.translation: They shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more; neither shall the sun light on them, nor any heat.

verses.original: ὅτι τὸ ἀρνίον τὸ ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ θρόνου ⸀ποιμανεῖ αὐτούς, καὶ ⸀ὁδηγήσει αὐτοὺς ἐπὶ ζωῆς πηγὰς ὑδάτων· καὶ ἐξαλείψει ὁ θεὸς πᾶν δάκρυον ἐκ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: oti to arnion to ana meson tou thronoy poimanei autoys, kai odigisei autous epi zoes pigas udaton* kai exaleipsei o theos pan dakryon ek ton ofthalmon auton.
verses.translation: For the Lamb which is in the midst of the throne shall feed them, and shall lead them unto living fountains of waters: and God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes.

verses.original: Καὶ ⸀ὅταν ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν ἑβδόμην, ἐγένετο σιγὴ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ὡς ἡμιώριον.
verses.translit: Kai otan enoixen ten sfragida ten evdomin, egeneto sige en to ourano os emiorion.
verses.translation: And when he had opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven about the space of half an hour.

verses.original: καὶ εἶδον τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλους οἳ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ ἑστήκασιν, καὶ ἐδόθησαν αὐτοῖς ἑπτὰ σάλπιγγες.
verses.translit: kai eidon tous epta aggeloys oi enopion tou theou estikasin, kai edothisan autois epta salpigges.
verses.translation: And I saw the seven angels which stood before God; and to them were given seven trumpets.

verses.original: Καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος ἦλθεν καὶ ἐστάθη ἐπὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου ἔχων λιβανωτὸν χρυσοῦν, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ θυμιάματα πολλὰ ἵνα ⸀δώσει ταῖς προσευχαῖς τῶν ἁγίων πάντων ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τὸ χρυσοῦν τὸ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου.
verses.translit: Kai allos aggelos elthen kai estathi epi tou thysiastirioy ehon livanoton hrysoun, kai edothi auto thymiamata polla ina dosei tais proseyhais ton agion panton epi to thysiastirion to hrysoun to enopion tou thronoy.
verses.translation: And another angel came and stood at the altar, having a golden censer; and there was given unto him much incense, that he should offer it with the prayers of all saints upon the golden altar which was before the throne.

verses.original: καὶ ἀνέβη ὁ καπνὸς τῶν θυμιαμάτων ταῖς προσευχαῖς τῶν ἁγίων ἐκ χειρὸς τοῦ ἀγγέλου ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: kai anevi o kapnos ton thymiamaton tais proseyhais ton agion ek heiros tou aggeloy enopion tou theou.
verses.translation: And the smoke of the incense, which came with the prayers of the saints, ascended up before God out of the angel’s hand.

verses.original: καὶ εἴληφεν ὁ ἄγγελος τὸν λιβανωτόν, καὶ ἐγέμισεν αὐτὸν ἐκ τοῦ πυρὸς τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, καὶ ἔβαλεν εἰς τὴν γῆν· καὶ ἐγένοντο βρονταὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ ἀστραπαὶ καὶ σεισμός.
verses.translit: kai eilifen o aggelos ton livanoton, kai egemisen auton ek tou pyros tou thysiastirioy, kai evalen eis ten gen* kai egenonto vrontai kai fonai kai astrapai kai seismos.
verses.translation: And the angel took the censer, and filled it with fire of the altar, and cast it into the earth: and there were voices, and thunderings, and lightnings, and an earthquake.

verses.original: Καὶ οἱ ἑπτὰ ἄγγελοι οἱ ἔχοντες τὰς ἑπτὰ σάλπιγγας ἡτοίμασαν ⸀αὑτοὺς ἵνα σαλπίσωσιν.
verses.translit: Kai oi epta aggeloi oi ehontes tas epta salpiggas etoimasan autous ina salpisosin.
verses.translation: And the seven angels which had the seven trumpets prepared themselves to sound.

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ πρῶτος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ἐγένετο χάλαζα καὶ πῦρ μεμιγμένα ἐν αἵματι, καὶ ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν γῆν· καὶ τὸ τρίτον τῆς γῆς κατεκάη, καὶ τὸ τρίτον τῶν δένδρων κατεκάη, καὶ πᾶς χόρτος χλωρὸς κατεκάη.
verses.translit: Kai o protos esalpisen* kai egeneto halaza kai pur memigmena en aimati, kai evlithi eis ten gen* kai to triton tes ges katekai, kai to triton ton dendron katekai, kai pas hortos hloros katekai.
verses.translation: The first angel sounded, and there followed hail and fire mingled with blood, and they were cast upon the earth: and the third part of trees was burnt up, and all green grass was burnt up.

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ δεύτερος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ὡς ὄρος μέγα ⸀πυρὶ καιόμενον ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν· καὶ ἐγένετο τὸ τρίτον τῆς θαλάσσης αἷμα,
verses.translit: Kai o deyteros aggelos esalpisen* kai os oros mega pyri kaiomenon evlithi eis ten thalassan* kai egeneto to triton tes thalassis aima,
verses.translation: And the second angel sounded, and as it were a great mountain burning with fire was cast into the sea: and the third part of the sea became blood;

verses.original: καὶ ἀπέθανε τὸ τρίτον ⸀τῶν κτισμάτων τῶν ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, τὰ ἔχοντα ψυχάς, καὶ τὸ τρίτον τῶν πλοίων ⸀διεφθάρησαν.
verses.translit: kai apethane to triton ton ktismaton ton en te thalasse, ta ehonta psyhas, kai to triton ton ploion dieftharisan.
verses.translation: And the third part of the creatures which were in the sea, and had life, died; and the third part of the ships were destroyed.

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ τρίτος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ἔπεσεν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀστὴρ μέγας καιόμενος ὡς λαμπάς, καὶ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὸ τρίτον τῶν ποταμῶν καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς πηγὰς τῶν ὑδάτων.
verses.translit: Kai o tritos aggelos esalpisen* kai epesen ek tou ouranou aster megas kaiomenos os lampas, kai epesen epi to triton ton potamon kai epi tas pigas ton udaton.
verses.translation: And the third angel sounded, and there fell a great star from heaven, burning as it were a lamp, and it fell upon the third part of the rivers, and upon the fountains of waters;

verses.original: καὶ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ ἀστέρος λέγεται· ⸀ὁ Ἄψινθος. καὶ ἐγένετο τὸ τρίτον τῶν ὑδάτων εἰς ἄψινθον, καὶ πολλοὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀπέθανον ἐκ τῶν ὑδάτων, ὅτι ἐπικράνθησαν.
verses.translit: kai to onoma tou asteros legetai* o Apsinthos. kai egeneto to triton ton udaton eis apsinthon, kai polloi ton anthropon apethanon ek ton udaton, oti epikranthisan.
verses.translation: And the name of the star is called Wormwood: and the third part of the waters became wormwood; and many men died of the waters, because they were made bitter.

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ τέταρτος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ἐπλήγη τὸ τρίτον τοῦ ἡλίου καὶ τὸ τρίτον τῆς σελήνης καὶ τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀστέρων, ἵνα σκοτισθῇ τὸ τρίτον αὐτῶν καὶ ⸂ἡ ἡμέρα μὴ φάνῃ τὸ τρίτον αὐτῆς⸃, καὶ ἡ νὺξ ὁμοίως.
verses.translit: Kai o tetartos aggelos esalpisen* kai epligi to triton tou elioy kai to triton tes selinis kai to triton ton asteron, ina skotisthe to triton auton kai e emera me fane to triton autes, kai e nux omoios.
verses.translation: And the fourth angel sounded, and the third part of the sun was smitten, and the third part of the moon, and the third part of the stars; so as the third part of them was darkened, and the day shone not for a third part of it, and the night likewise.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἤκουσα ἑνὸς ἀετοῦ πετομένου ἐν μεσουρανήματι λέγοντος φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Οὐαὶ οὐαὶ οὐαὶ ⸂τοὺς κατοικοῦντας⸃ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἐκ τῶν λοιπῶν φωνῶν τῆς σάλπιγγος τῶν τριῶν ἀγγέλων τῶν μελλόντων σαλπίζειν.
verses.translit: Kai eidon, kai ekoysa enos aetou petomenoy en mesoyranimati legontos fone megale* Ouai ouai ouai tous katoikountas epi tes ges ek ton loipon fonon tes salpiggos ton trion aggelon ton mellonton salpizein.
verses.translation: And I beheld, and heard an angel flying through the midst of heaven, saying with a loud voice, Woe, woe, woe, to the inhabiters of the earth by reason of the other voices of the trumpet of the three angels, which are yet to sound!

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ πέμπτος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ εἶδον ἀστέρα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ πεπτωκότα εἰς τὴν γῆν, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ἡ κλεὶς τοῦ φρέατος τῆς ἀβύσσου·
verses.translit: Kai o pemptos aggelos esalpisen* kai eidon astera ek tou ouranou peptokota eis ten gen, kai edothi auto e kleis tou freatos tes avyssoy*
verses.translation: And the fifth angel sounded, and I saw a star fall from heaven unto the earth: and to him was given the key of the bottomless pit.

verses.original: καὶ ἤνοιξεν τὸ φρέαρ τῆς ἀβύσσου, καὶ ἀνέβη καπνὸς ἐκ τοῦ φρέατος ὡς καπνὸς καμίνου ⸀μεγάλης, καὶ ⸀ἐσκοτώθη ὁ ἥλιος καὶ ὁ ἀὴρ ἐκ τοῦ καπνοῦ τοῦ φρέατος.
verses.translit: kai enoixen to frear tes avyssoy, kai anevi kapnos ek tou freatos os kapnos kaminoy megalis, kai eskotothi o elios kai o aer ek tou kapnou tou freatos.
verses.translation: And he opened the bottomless pit; and there arose a smoke out of the pit, as the smoke of a great furnace; and the sun and the air were darkened by reason of the smoke of the pit.

verses.original: καὶ ἐκ τοῦ καπνοῦ ἐξῆλθον ἀκρίδες εἰς τὴν γῆν, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐταῖς ἐξουσία ὡς ἔχουσιν ἐξουσίαν οἱ σκορπίοι τῆς γῆς.
verses.translit: kai ek tou kapnou exelthon akrides eis ten gen, kai edothi autais exoysia os ehoysin exoysian oi skorpioi tes ges.
verses.translation: And there came out of the smoke locusts upon the earth: and unto them was given power, as the scorpions of the earth have power.

verses.original: καὶ ἐρρέθη αὐταῖς ἵνα μὴ ⸀ἀδικήσουσιν τὸν χόρτον τῆς γῆς οὐδὲ πᾶν χλωρὸν οὐδὲ πᾶν δένδρον, εἰ μὴ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους οἵτινες οὐκ ἔχουσι τὴν σφραγῖδα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ τῶν ⸀μετώπων.
verses.translit: kai errethi autais ina me adikisoysin ton horton tes ges oude pan hloron oude pan dendron, ei me tous anthropoys oitines ouk ehoysi ten sfragida tou theou epi ton metopon.
verses.translation: And it was commanded them that they should not hurt the grass of the earth, neither any green thing, neither any tree; but only those men which have not the seal of God in their foreheads.

verses.original: καὶ ἐδόθη ⸀αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ ἀποκτείνωσιν αὐτούς, ἀλλʼ ἵνα ⸀βασανισθήσονται μῆνας πέντε· καὶ ὁ βασανισμὸς αὐτῶν ὡς βασανισμὸς σκορπίου, ὅταν παίσῃ ἄνθρωπον.
verses.translit: kai edothi autois ina me apokteinosin autoys, all' ina vasanisthisontai menas pente* kai o vasanismos auton os vasanismos skorpioy, otan paise anthropon.
verses.translation: And to them it was given that they should not kill them, but that they should be tormented five months: and their torment was as the torment of a scorpion, when he striketh a man.

verses.original: καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ζητήσουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι τὸν θάνατον καὶ οὐ μὴ εὑρήσουσιν αὐτόν, καὶ ἐπιθυμήσουσιν ἀποθανεῖν καὶ ⸀φεύγει ⸂ὁ θάνατος ἀπʼ αὐτῶν⸃.
verses.translit: kai en tais emerais ekeinais zitisoysin oi anthropoi ton thanaton kai ou me eurisoysin auton, kai epithymisoysin apothanein kai feygei o thanatos ap' auton.
verses.translation: And in those days shall men seek death, and shall not find it; and shall desire to die, and death shall flee from them.

verses.original: Καὶ τὰ ὁμοιώματα τῶν ἀκρίδων ὅμοια ἵπποις ἡτοιμασμένοις εἰς πόλεμον, καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν ὡς στέφανοι ⸂ὅμοιοι χρυσῷ⸃, καὶ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὡς πρόσωπα ἀνθρώπων,
verses.translit: Kai ta omoiomata ton akridon omoia ippois etoimasmenois eis polemon, kai epi tas kefalas auton os stefanoi omoioi hryso, kai ta prosopa auton os prosopa anthropon,
verses.translation: And the shapes of the locusts were like unto horses prepared unto battle; and on their heads were as it were crowns like gold, and their faces were as the faces of men.

verses.original: καὶ εἶχον τρίχας ὡς τρίχας γυναικῶν, καὶ οἱ ὀδόντες αὐτῶν ὡς λεόντων ἦσαν,
verses.translit: kai eihon trihas os trihas gynaikon, kai oi odontes auton os leonton esan,
verses.translation: And they had hair as the hair of women, and their teeth were as the teeth of lions.

verses.original: καὶ εἶχον θώρακας ὡς θώρακας σιδηροῦς, καὶ ἡ φωνὴ τῶν πτερύγων αὐτῶν ὡς φωνὴ ἁρμάτων ἵππων πολλῶν τρεχόντων εἰς πόλεμον·
verses.translit: kai eihon thorakas os thorakas sidirous, kai e fone ton pterygon auton os fone armaton ippon pollon trehonton eis polemon*
verses.translation: And they had breastplates, as it were breastplates of iron; and the sound of their wings was as the sound of chariots of many horses running to battle.

verses.original: καὶ ἔχουσιν οὐρὰς ὁμοίας σκορπίοις καὶ κέντρα, καὶ ἐν ταῖς οὐραῖς αὐτῶν ⸂ἡ ἐξουσία αὐτῶν⸃ ἀδικῆσαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους μῆνας πέντε.
verses.translit: kai ehoysin ouras omoias skorpiois kai kentra, kai en tais ourais auton e exoysia auton adikesai tous anthropoys menas pente.
verses.translation: And they had tails like unto scorpions, and there were stings in their tails: and their power was to hurt men five months.

verses.original: ⸂ἔχουσιν ἐπʼ αὐτῶν βασιλέα τὸν⸃ ἄγγελον τῆς ἀβύσσου· ὄνομα αὐτῷ Ἑβραϊστὶ Ἀβαδδών, ⸂καὶ ἐν⸃ τῇ Ἑλληνικῇ ὄνομα ἔχει Ἀπολλύων.
verses.translit: ehoysin ep' auton vasilea ton aggelon tes avyssoy* onoma auto Evraisti Avaddon, kai en te Ellinike onoma ehei Apollyon.
verses.translation: And they had a king over them, which is the angel of the bottomless pit, whose name in the Hebrew tongue is Abaddon, but in the Greek tongue hath his name Apollyon.

verses.original: Ἡ οὐαὶ ἡ μία ἀπῆλθεν· ἰδοὺ ἔρχεται ἔτι δύο οὐαὶ μετὰ ταῦτα.
verses.translit: E ouai e mia apelthen* idou erhetai eti dyo ouai meta tauta.
verses.translation: One woe is past; and , behold, there come two woes more hereafter.

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ ἕκτος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν μίαν ἐκ ⸀τῶν κεράτων τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τοῦ χρυσοῦ τοῦ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ,
verses.translit: Kai o ektos aggelos esalpisen* kai ekoysa fonen mian ek ton keraton tou thysiastirioy tou hrysou tou enopion tou theou,
verses.translation: And the sixth angel sounded, and I heard a voice from the four horns of the golden altar which is before God,

verses.original: ⸀λέγοντα τῷ ἕκτῳ ἀγγέλῳ, ὁ ἔχων τὴν σάλπιγγα· Λῦσον τοὺς τέσσαρας ἀγγέλους τοὺς δεδεμένους ἐπὶ τῷ ποταμῷ τῷ μεγάλῳ Εὐφράτῃ.
verses.translit: legonta to ekto aggelo, o ehon ten salpigga* Luson tous tessaras aggeloys tous dedemenoys epi to potamo to megalo Eufrate.
verses.translation: Saying to the sixth angel which had the trumpet, Loose the four angels which are bound in the great river Euphrates.

verses.original: καὶ ἐλύθησαν οἱ τέσσαρες ἄγγελοι οἱ ἡτοιμασμένοι εἰς τὴν ὥραν ⸀καὶ ἡμέραν καὶ μῆνα καὶ ἐνιαυτόν, ἵνα ἀποκτείνωσιν τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
verses.translit: kai elythisan oi tessares aggeloi oi etoimasmenoi eis ten oran kai emeran kai mena kai eniayton, ina apokteinosin to triton ton anthropon.
verses.translation: And the four angels were loosed, which were prepared for an hour, and a day, and a month, and a year, for to slay the third part of men.

verses.original: καὶ ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν στρατευμάτων τοῦ ⸀ἱππικοῦ ⸀δισμυριάδες μυριάδων· ἤκουσα τὸν ἀριθμὸν αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai o arithmos ton strateymaton tou ippikou dismyriades myriadon* ekoysa ton arithmon auton.
verses.translation: And the number of the army of the horsemen were two hundred thousand thousand: and I heard the number of them.

verses.original: καὶ οὕτως εἶδον τοὺς ἵππους ἐν τῇ ὁράσει καὶ τοὺς καθημένους ἐπʼ αὐτῶν, ἔχοντας θώρακας πυρίνους καὶ ὑακινθίνους καὶ θειώδεις· καὶ αἱ κεφαλαὶ τῶν ἵππων ὡς κεφαλαὶ λεόντων, καὶ ἐκ τῶν στομάτων αὐτῶν ἐκπορεύεται πῦρ καὶ καπνὸς καὶ θεῖον.
verses.translit: kai outos eidon tous ippoys en te orasei kai tous kathimenoys ep' auton, ehontas thorakas pyrinoys kai uakinthinoys kai theiodeis* kai ai kefalai ton ippon os kefalai leonton, kai ek ton stomaton auton ekporeyetai pur kai kapnos kai theion.
verses.translation: And thus I saw the horses in the vision, and them that sat on them, having breastplates of fire, and of jacinth, and brimstone: and the heads of the horses were as the heads of lions; and out of their mouths issued fire and smoke and brimstone.

verses.original: ἀπὸ τῶν τριῶν πληγῶν τούτων ἀπεκτάνθησαν τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ⸀ἐκ τοῦ πυρὸς καὶ τοῦ καπνοῦ καὶ τοῦ θείου τοῦ ἐκπορευομένου ἐκ τῶν στομάτων αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: apo ton trion pligon toyton apektanthisan to triton ton anthropon, ek tou pyros kai tou kapnou kai tou theioy tou ekporeyomenoy ek ton stomaton auton.
verses.translation: By these three was the third part of men killed, by the fire, and by the smoke, and by the brimstone, which issued out of their mouths.

verses.original: ἡ γὰρ ἐξουσία τῶν ἵππων ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτῶν ἐστιν καὶ ἐν ταῖς οὐραῖς αὐτῶν· αἱ γὰρ οὐραὶ αὐτῶν ὅμοιαι ⸀ὄφεσιν, ἔχουσαι κεφαλάς, καὶ ἐν αὐταῖς ἀδικοῦσιν.
verses.translit: e gar exoysia ton ippon en to stomati auton estin kai en tais ourais auton* ai gar ourai auton omoiai ofesin, ehoysai kefalas, kai en autais adikousin.
verses.translation: For their power is in their mouth, and in their tails: for their tails were like unto serpents, and had heads, and with them they do hurt.

verses.original: Καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, οἳ οὐκ ἀπεκτάνθησαν ἐν ταῖς πληγαῖς ταύταις, ⸀οὐδὲ μετενόησαν ἐκ τῶν ἔργων τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν, ἵνα μὴ ⸀προσκυνήσουσιν τὰ δαιμόνια καὶ τὰ εἴδωλα τὰ χρυσᾶ καὶ τὰ ἀργυρᾶ καὶ τὰ χαλκᾶ καὶ τὰ λίθινα καὶ τὰ ξύλινα, ἃ οὔτε βλέπειν ⸀δύνανται οὔτε ἀκούειν οὔτε περιπατεῖν,
verses.translit: Kai oi loipoi ton anthropon, oi ouk apektanthisan en tais pligais taytais, oude metenoisan ek ton ergon ton heiron auton, ina me proskynisoysin ta daimonia kai ta eidola ta hrysa kai ta argyra kai ta halka kai ta lithina kai ta xylina, a oute vlepein dynantai oute akoyein oute peripatein,
verses.translation: And the rest of the men which were not killed by these plagues yet repented not of the works of their hands, that they should not worship devils, and idols of gold, and silver, and brass, and stone, and of wood: which neither can see, nor hear, nor walk:

verses.original: καὶ οὐ μετενόησαν ἐκ τῶν φόνων αὐτῶν οὔτε ἐκ τῶν ⸀φαρμάκων αὐτῶν οὔτε ἐκ τῆς πορνείας αὐτῶν οὔτε ἐκ τῶν κλεμμάτων αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai ou metenoisan ek ton fonon auton oute ek ton farmakon auton oute ek tes porneias auton oute ek ton klemmaton auton.
verses.translation: Neither repented they of their murders, nor of their sorceries, nor of their fornication, nor of their thefts.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶδον ⸀ἄλλον ἄγγελον ἰσχυρὸν καταβαίνοντα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, περιβεβλημένον νεφέλην, καὶ ἡ ἶρις ἐπὶ ⸂τὴν κεφαλὴν⸃ αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος, καὶ οἱ πόδες αὐτοῦ ὡς στῦλοι πυρός,
verses.translit: Kai eidon allon aggelon ishyron katavainonta ek tou ouranou, perivevlimenon nefelin, kai e iris epi ten kefalen autou, kai to prosopon autou os o elios, kai oi podes autou os stuloi pyros,
verses.translation: And I saw another mighty angel come down from heaven, clothed with a cloud: and a rainbow was upon his head, and his face was as it were the sun, and his feet as pillars of fire:

verses.original: καὶ ἔχων ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ ⸀βιβλαρίδιον ἠνεῳγμένον. καὶ ἔθηκεν τὸν πόδα αὐτοῦ τὸν δεξιὸν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης, τὸν δὲ εὐώνυμον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς,
verses.translit: kai ehon en te heiri autou vivlaridion eneogmenon. kai ethiken ton poda autou ton dexion epi tes thalassis, ton de euonymon epi tes ges,
verses.translation: And he had in his hand a little book open: and he set his right foot upon the sea, and his left foot on the earth,

verses.original: καὶ ἔκραξεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ὥσπερ λέων μυκᾶται. καὶ ὅτε ἔκραξεν, ἐλάλησαν αἱ ἑπτὰ βρονταὶ τὰς ἑαυτῶν φωνάς.
verses.translit: kai ekraxen fone megale osper leon mykatai. kai ote ekraxen, elalisan ai epta vrontai tas eayton fonas.
verses.translation: And cried with a loud voice, as when a lion roareth: and when he had cried, seven thunders uttered their voices.

verses.original: καὶ ὅτε ἐλάλησαν αἱ ἑπτὰ βρονταί, ἤμελλον γράφειν· καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ λέγουσαν· Σφράγισον ἃ ἐλάλησαν αἱ ἑπτὰ βρονταί, καὶ μὴ αὐτὰ γράψῃς.
verses.translit: kai ote elalisan ai epta vrontai, emellon grafein* kai ekoysa fonen ek tou ouranou legoysan* Sfragison a elalisan ai epta vrontai, kai me auta grapses.
verses.translation: And when the seven thunders had uttered their voices, I was about to write: and I heard a voice from heaven saying unto me, Seal up those things which the seven thunders uttered, and write them not.

verses.original: καὶ ὁ ἄγγελος, ὃν εἶδον ἑστῶτα ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ἦρεν τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ τὴν δεξιὰν εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν,
verses.translit: kai o aggelos, on eidon estota epi tes thalassis kai epi tes ges, eren ten heira autou ten dexian eis ton ouranon,
verses.translation: And the angel which I saw stand upon the sea and upon the earth lifted up his hand to heaven,

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ὤμοσεν τῷ ζῶντι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, ὃς ἔκτισεν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ, ὅτι χρόνος οὐκέτι ἔσται·
verses.translit: kai omosen to zonti eis tous aionas ton aionon, os ektisen ton ouranon kai ta en auto kai ten gen kai ta en aute kai ten thalassan kai ta en aute, oti hronos ouketi estai*
verses.translation: And sware by him that liveth for ever and ever, who created heaven, and the things that therein are, and the earth, and the things that therein are, and the sea, and the things which are therein, that there should be time no longer:

verses.original: ἀλλʼ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῆς φωνῆς τοῦ ἑβδόμου ἀγγέλου, ὅταν μέλλῃ σαλπίζειν, καὶ ἐτελέσθη τὸ μυστήριον τοῦ θεοῦ, ὡς εὐηγγέλισεν τοὺς ⸂ἑαυτοῦ δούλους⸃ τοὺς προφήτας.
verses.translit: all' en tais emerais tes fones tou evdomoy aggeloy, otan melle salpizein, kai etelesthi to mystirion tou theou, os euiggelisen tous eaytou doyloys tous profitas.
verses.translation: But in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he shall begin to sound, the mystery of God should be finished, as he hath declared to his servants the prophets.

verses.original: Καὶ ἡ φωνὴ ἣν ἤκουσα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, πάλιν ⸀λαλοῦσαν μετʼ ἐμοῦ καὶ ⸀λέγουσαν· Ὕπαγε λάβε τὸ ⸀βιβλίον τὸ ἠνεῳγμένον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ τοῦ ἀγγέλου τοῦ ἑστῶτος ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
verses.translit: Kai e fone en ekoysa ek tou ouranou, palin lalousan met' emou kai legoysan* Upage lave to vivlion to eneogmenon en te heiri tou aggeloy tou estotos epi tes thalassis kai epi tes ges.
verses.translation: And the voice which I heard from heaven spake unto me again, and said, Go and take the little book which is open in the hand of the angel which standeth upon the sea and upon the earth.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ἀπῆλθα πρὸς τὸν ἄγγελον λέγων αὐτῷ δοῦναί μοι τὸ ⸀βιβλαρίδιον. καὶ λέγει μοι· Λάβε καὶ κατάφαγε αὐτό, καὶ πικρανεῖ σου τὴν κοιλίαν, ἀλλʼ ἐν τῷ στόματί σου ἔσται γλυκὺ ὡς μέλι.
verses.translit: kai apeltha pros ton aggelon legon auto dounai moi to vivlaridion. kai legei moi* Lave kai katafage auto, kai pikranei soy ten koilian, all' en to stomati soy estai glyku os meli.
verses.translation: And I went unto the angel, and said unto him, Give me the little book. And he said unto me, Take it , and eat it up; and it shall make thy belly bitter, but it shall be in thy mouth sweet as honey.

verses.original: καὶ ἔλαβον τὸ ⸀βιβλαρίδιον ἐκ τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ ἀγγέλου καὶ κατέφαγον αὐτό, καὶ ἦν ἐν τῷ στόματί μου ὡς μέλι γλυκύ· καὶ ὅτε ἔφαγον αὐτό, ἐπικράνθη ἡ κοιλία μου.
verses.translit: kai elavon to vivlaridion ek tes heiros tou aggeloy kai katefagon auto, kai en en to stomati moy os meli glyky* kai ote efagon auto, epikranthi e koilia moy.
verses.translation: And I took the little book out of the angel’s hand, and ate it up; and it was in my mouth sweet as honey: and as soon as I had eaten it, my belly was bitter.

verses.original: Καὶ λέγουσίν μοι· Δεῖ σε πάλιν προφητεῦσαι ἐπὶ λαοῖς ⸀καὶ ἔθνεσιν καὶ γλώσσαις καὶ βασιλεῦσιν πολλοῖς.
verses.translit: Kai legoysin moi* Dei se palin profiteusai epi laois kai ethnesin kai glossais kai vasileusin pollois.
verses.translation: And he said unto me, Thou must prophesy again before many peoples, and nations, and tongues, and kings.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐδόθη μοι κάλαμος ὅμοιος ῥάβδῳ, λέγων· ⸀Ἔγειρε καὶ μέτρησον τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον καὶ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας ἐν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: Kai edothi moi kalamos omoios Ravdo, legon* Egeire kai metrison ton naon tou theou kai to thysiastirion kai tous proskynountas en auto.
verses.translation: And there was given me a reed like unto a rod: and the angel stood, saying, Rise, and measure the temple of God, and the altar, and them that worship therein.

verses.original: καὶ τὴν αὐλὴν τὴν ἔξωθεν τοῦ ναοῦ ἔκβαλε ⸀ἔξωθεν, καὶ μὴ αὐτὴν μετρήσῃς, ὅτι ἐδόθη τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, καὶ τὴν πόλιν τὴν ἁγίαν πατήσουσιν μῆνας ⸀τεσσεράκοντα δύο.
verses.translit: kai ten aulen ten exothen tou naou ekvale exothen, kai me auten metrises, oti edothi tois ethnesin, kai ten polin ten agian patisoysin menas tesserakonta dyo.
verses.translation: But the court which is without the temple leave out, and measure it not; for it is given unto the Gentiles: and the holy city shall they tread under foot forty and two months.

verses.original: καὶ δώσω τοῖς δυσὶν μάρτυσίν μου, καὶ προφητεύσουσιν ἡμέρας χιλίας διακοσίας ἑξήκοντα, ⸀περιβεβλημένοι σάκκους.
verses.translit: kai doso tois dysin martysin moy, kai profiteysoysin emeras hilias diakosias exikonta, perivevlimenoi sakkoys.
verses.translation: And I will give power unto my two witnesses, and they shall prophesy a thousand two hundred and threescore days, clothed in sackcloth.

verses.original: Οὗτοί εἰσιν αἱ δύο ἐλαῖαι καὶ αἱ δύο λυχνίαι αἱ ἐνώπιον τοῦ κυρίου τῆς γῆς ⸀ἑστῶτες.
verses.translit: Outoi eisin ai dyo elaiai kai ai dyo lyhniai ai enopion tou kyrioy tes ges estotes.
verses.translation: These are the two olive trees, and the two candlesticks standing before the God of the earth.

verses.original: καὶ εἴ τις αὐτοὺς θέλει ἀδικῆσαι, πῦρ ἐκπορεύεται ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτῶν καὶ κατεσθίει τοὺς ἐχθροὺς αὐτῶν· καὶ εἴ τις ⸂θελήσῃ αὐτοὺς⸃ ἀδικῆσαι, οὕτως δεῖ αὐτὸν ἀποκτανθῆναι.
verses.translit: kai ei tis autous thelei adikesai, pur ekporeyetai ek tou stomatos auton kai katesthiei tous ehthrous auton* kai ei tis thelise autous adikesai, outos dei auton apoktanthenai.
verses.translation: And if any man will hurt them, fire proceedeth out of their mouth, and devoureth their enemies: and if any man will hurt them, he must in this manner be killed.

verses.original: οὗτοι ἔχουσιν ⸂τὴν ἐξουσίαν κλεῖσαι τὸν οὐρανόν⸃, ἵνα μὴ ὑετὸς βρέχῃ τὰς ἡμέρας τῆς προφητείας αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἔχουσιν ἐπὶ τῶν ὑδάτων στρέφειν αὐτὰ εἰς αἷμα καὶ πατάξαι τὴν γῆν ⸂ἐν πάσῃ πληγῇ ὁσάκις ἐὰν θελήσωσιν⸃.
verses.translit: outoi ehoysin ten exoysian kleisai ton ouranon, ina me uetos vrehe tas emeras tes profiteias auton, kai exoysian ehoysin epi ton udaton strefein auta eis aima kai pataxai ten gen en pase plige osakis ean thelisosin.
verses.translation: These have power to shut heaven, that it rain not in the days of their prophecy: and have power over waters to turn them to blood, and to smite the earth with all plagues, as often as they will.

verses.original: Καὶ ὅταν τελέσωσιν τὴν μαρτυρίαν αὐτῶν, τὸ θηρίον τὸ ἀναβαῖνον ἐκ τῆς ἀβύσσου ποιήσει μετʼ αὐτῶν πόλεμον καὶ νικήσει αὐτοὺς καὶ ἀποκτενεῖ αὐτούς.
verses.translit: Kai otan telesosin ten martyrian auton, to thirion to anavainon ek tes avyssoy poiisei met' auton polemon kai nikisei autous kai apoktenei autoys.
verses.translation: And when they shall have finished their testimony, the beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit shall make war against them, and shall overcome them, and kill them.

verses.original: καὶ τὸ πτῶμα αὐτῶν ἐπὶ τῆς πλατείας τῆς πόλεως τῆς μεγάλης, ἥτις καλεῖται πνευματικῶς Σόδομα καὶ Αἴγυπτος, ὅπου καὶ ὁ κύριος αὐτῶν ἐσταυρώθη.
verses.translit: kai to ptoma auton epi tes plateias tes poleos tes megalis, etis kaleitai pneymatikos Sodoma kai Aigyptos, opoy kai o kyrios auton estayrothi.
verses.translation: And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.

verses.original: καὶ βλέπουσιν ἐκ τῶν λαῶν καὶ φυλῶν καὶ γλωσσῶν καὶ ἐθνῶν τὸ πτῶμα αὐτῶν ἡμέρας τρεῖς ⸀καὶ ἥμισυ, καὶ τὰ πτώματα αὐτῶν οὐκ ⸀ἀφίουσιν τεθῆναι εἰς μνῆμα.
verses.translit: kai vlepoysin ek ton laon kai fylon kai glosson kai ethnon to ptoma auton emeras treis kai emisy, kai ta ptomata auton ouk afioysin tethenai eis mnema.
verses.translation: And they of the people and kindreds and tongues and nations shall see their dead bodies three days and an half, and shall not suffer their dead bodies to be put in graves.

verses.original: καὶ οἱ κατοικοῦντες ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς χαίρουσιν ἐπʼ αὐτοῖς καὶ ⸀εὐφραίνονται, καὶ δῶρα ⸀πέμψουσιν ἀλλήλοις, ὅτι οὗτοι οἱ δύο προφῆται ἐβασάνισαν τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
verses.translit: kai oi katoikountes epi tes ges hairoysin ep' autois kai eufrainontai, kai dora pempsoysin allilois, oti outoi oi dyo profetai evasanisan tous katoikountas epi tes ges.
verses.translation: And they that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another; because these two prophets tormented them that dwelt on the earth.

verses.original: Καὶ μετὰ τὰς τρεῖς ἡμέρας καὶ ἥμισυ πνεῦμα ζωῆς ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσῆλθεν ⸂ἐν αὐτοῖς⸃, καὶ ἔστησαν ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας αὐτῶν, καὶ φόβος μέγας ⸀ἐπέπεσεν ἐπὶ τοὺς θεωροῦντας αὐτούς·
verses.translit: Kai meta tas treis emeras kai emisy pneuma zoes ek tou theou eiselthen en autois, kai estisan epi tous podas auton, kai fovos megas epepesen epi tous theorountas autoys*
verses.translation: And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ἤκουσαν ⸂φωνῆς μεγάλης⸃ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ⸀λεγούσης αὐτοῖς· ⸀Ἀνάβατε ὧδε, καὶ ἀνέβησαν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἐν τῇ νεφέλῃ, καὶ ἐθεώρησαν αὐτοὺς οἱ ἐχθροὶ αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai ekoysan fones megalis ek tou ouranou legoysis autois* Anavate ode, kai anevisan eis ton ouranon en te nefele, kai etheorisan autous oi ehthroi auton.
verses.translation: And they heard a great voice from heaven saying unto them, Come up hither. And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud; and their enemies beheld them.

verses.original: καὶ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ⸀ὥρᾳ ἐγένετο σεισμὸς μέγας, καὶ τὸ δέκατον τῆς πόλεως ἔπεσεν, καὶ ἀπεκτάνθησαν ἐν τῷ σεισμῷ ὀνόματα ἀνθρώπων χιλιάδες ἑπτά, καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ ἔμφοβοι ἐγένοντο καὶ ἔδωκαν δόξαν τῷ θεῷ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
verses.translit: kai en ekeine te ora egeneto seismos megas, kai to dekaton tes poleos epesen, kai apektanthisan en to seismo onomata anthropon hiliades epta, kai oi loipoi emfovoi egenonto kai edokan doxan to theo tou ouranou.
verses.translation: And the same hour was there a great earthquake, and the tenth part of the city fell, and in the earthquake were slain of men seven thousand: and the remnant were affrighted, and gave glory to the God of heaven.

verses.original: Ἡ οὐαὶ ἡ δευτέρα ἀπῆλθεν· ⸂ἰδοὺ ἡ οὐαὶ ἡ τρίτη⸃ ἔρχεται ταχύ.
verses.translit: E ouai e deytera apelthen* idou e ouai e triti erhetai tahy.
verses.translation: The second woe is past; and , behold, the third woe cometh quickly.

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ ἕβδομος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ἐγένοντο φωναὶ μεγάλαι ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ⸀λέγοντες· Ἐγένετο ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ κόσμου τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν καὶ τοῦ χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ, καὶ βασιλεύσει εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων.
verses.translit: Kai o evdomos aggelos esalpisen* kai egenonto fonai megalai en to ourano legontes* Egeneto e vasileia tou kosmoy tou kyrioy emon kai tou hristou autou, kai vasileysei eis tous aionas ton aionon.
verses.translation: And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever.

verses.original: Καὶ οἱ εἴκοσι τέσσαρες πρεσβύτεροι οἱ ἐνώπιον τοῦ ⸂θεοῦ καθήμενοι⸃ ἐπὶ τοὺς θρόνους αὐτῶν ἔπεσαν ἐπὶ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ θεῷ,
verses.translit: Kai oi eikosi tessares presvyteroi oi enopion tou theou kathimenoi epi tous thronoys auton epesan epi ta prosopa auton kai prosekynisan to theo,
verses.translation: And the four and twenty elders, which sat before God on their seats, fell upon their faces, and worshipped God,

verses.original: λέγοντες· Εὐχαριστοῦμέν σοι, κύριε, ὁ θεός, ὁ παντοκράτωρ, ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν, ὅτι εἴληφας τὴν δύναμίν σου τὴν μεγάλην καὶ ἐβασίλευσας.
verses.translit: legontes* Euharistoumen soi, kyrie, o theos, o pantokrator, o on kai o en, oti eilifas ten dynamin soy ten megalin kai evasileysas.
verses.translation: Saying, We give thee thanks, O Lord God Almighty, which art, and wast, and art to come; because thou hast taken to thee thy great power, and hast reigned.

verses.original: καὶ τὰ ἔθνη ὠργίσθησαν, καὶ ἦλθεν ἡ ὀργή σου καὶ ὁ καιρὸς τῶν νεκρῶν κριθῆναι καὶ δοῦναι τὸν μισθὸν τοῖς δούλοις σου τοῖς προφήταις καὶ τοῖς ἁγίοις καὶ τοῖς φοβουμένοις τὸ ὄνομά σου, ⸂τοὺς μικροὺς καὶ τοὺς μεγάλους⸃, καὶ διαφθεῖραι τοὺς διαφθείροντας τὴν γῆν.
verses.translit: kai ta ethni orgisthisan, kai elthen e orgi soy kai o kairos ton nekron krithenai kai dounai ton misthon tois doylois soy tois profitais kai tois agiois kai tois fovoymenois to onoma soy, tous mikrous kai tous megaloys, kai diaftheirai tous diaftheirontas ten gen.
verses.translation: And the nations were angry, and thy wrath is come, and the time of the dead, that they should be judged, and that thou shouldest give reward unto thy servants the prophets, and to the saints, and them that fear thy name, small and great; and shouldest destroy them which destroy the earth.

verses.original: Καὶ ἠνοίγη ὁ ναὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ⸀ὁ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ ὤφθη ἡ κιβωτὸς τῆς διαθήκης ⸀αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ ναῷ αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἐγένοντο ἀστραπαὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ βρονταὶ ⸂καὶ σεισμὸς⸃ καὶ χάλαζα μεγάλη.
verses.translit: Kai enoigi o naos tou theou o en to ourano, kai ofthi e kivotos tes diathikis autou en to nao autou* kai egenonto astrapai kai fonai kai vrontai kai seismos kai halaza megali.
verses.translation: And the temple of God was opened in heaven, and there was seen in his temple the ark of his testament: and there were lightnings, and voices, and thunderings, and an earthquake, and great hail.

verses.original: Καὶ σημεῖον μέγα ὤφθη ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, γυνὴ περιβεβλημένη τὸν ἥλιον, καὶ ἡ σελήνη ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν αὐτῆς, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτῆς στέφανος ἀστέρων δώδεκα,
verses.translit: Kai simeion mega ofthi en to ourano, gyne perivevlimeni ton elion, kai e selini upokato ton podon autes, kai epi tes kefales autes stefanos asteron dodeka,
verses.translation: And there appeared a great wonder in heaven; a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and upon her head a crown of twelve stars:

verses.original: καὶ ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα· ⸂καὶ κράζει⸃ ὠδίνουσα καὶ βασανιζομένη τεκεῖν.
verses.translit: kai en gastri ehoysa* kai krazei odinoysa kai vasanizomeni tekein.
verses.translation: And she being with child cried, travailing in birth, and pained to be delivered.

verses.original: καὶ ὤφθη ἄλλο σημεῖον ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ ἰδοὺ δράκων ⸂μέγας πυρρός⸃, ἔχων κεφαλὰς ἑπτὰ καὶ κέρατα δέκα καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτοῦ ἑπτὰ διαδήματα,
verses.translit: kai ofthi allo simeion en to ourano, kai idou drakon megas pyrros, ehon kefalas epta kai kerata deka kai epi tas kefalas autou epta diadimata,
verses.translation: And there appeared another wonder in heaven; and behold a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns upon his heads.

verses.original: καὶ ἡ οὐρὰ αὐτοῦ σύρει τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀστέρων τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἔβαλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν γῆν. καὶ ὁ δράκων ἕστηκεν ἐνώπιον τῆς γυναικὸς τῆς μελλούσης τεκεῖν, ἵνα ὅταν τέκῃ τὸ τέκνον αὐτῆς καταφάγῃ.
verses.translit: kai e oura autou syrei to triton ton asteron tou ouranou, kai evalen autous eis ten gen. kai o drakon estiken enopion tes gynaikos tes melloysis tekein, ina otan teke to teknon autes katafage.
verses.translation: And his tail drew the third part of the stars of heaven, and did cast them to the earth: and the dragon stood before the woman which was ready to be delivered, for to devour her child as soon as it was born.

verses.original: καὶ ἔτεκεν υἱόν, ⸀ἄρσεν, ὃς μέλλει ποιμαίνειν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἐν ῥάβδῳ σιδηρᾷ· καὶ ἡρπάσθη τὸ τέκνον αὐτῆς πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ πρὸς τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai eteken yion, arsen, os mellei poimainein panta ta ethni en Ravdo sidira* kai erpasthi to teknon autes pros ton theon kai pros ton thronon autou.
verses.translation: And she brought forth a man child, who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron: and her child was caught up unto God, and to his throne.

verses.original: καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἔφυγεν εἰς τὴν ἔρημον, ὅπου ἔχει ἐκεῖ τόπον ἡτοιμασμένον ⸀ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἵνα ἐκεῖ ⸀τρέφωσιν αὐτὴν ἡμέρας χιλίας διακοσίας ἑξήκοντα.
verses.translit: kai e gyne efygen eis ten erimon, opoy ehei ekei topon etoimasmenon apo tou theou, ina ekei trefosin auten emeras hilias diakosias exikonta.
verses.translation: And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she hath a place prepared of God, that they should feed her there a thousand two hundred and threescore days.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο πόλεμος ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ὁ Μιχαὴλ καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ ⸀τοῦ πολεμῆσαι μετὰ τοῦ δράκοντος. καὶ ὁ δράκων ἐπολέμησεν καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: Kai egeneto polemos en to ourano, o Mihael kai oi aggeloi autou tou polemesai meta tou drakontos. kai o drakon epolemisen kai oi aggeloi autou,
verses.translation: And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon; and the dragon fought and his angels,

verses.original: καὶ οὐκ ⸀ἴσχυσεν, οὐδὲ τόπος εὑρέθη ⸀αὐτῶν ἔτι ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ.
verses.translit: kai ouk ishysen, oude topos eurethi auton eti en to ourano.
verses.translation: And prevailed not; neither was their place found any more in heaven.

verses.original: καὶ ἐβλήθη ὁ δράκων ὁ μέγας, ὁ ὄφις ὁ ἀρχαῖος, ὁ καλούμενος Διάβολος καὶ ⸀ὁ Σατανᾶς, ὁ πλανῶν τὴν οἰκουμένην ὅλην— ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν γῆν, καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ἐβλήθησαν.
verses.translit: kai evlithi o drakon o megas, o ofis o arhaios, o kaloymenos Diavolos kai o Satanas, o planon ten oikoymenin olin-- evlithi eis ten gen, kai oi aggeloi autou met' autou evlithisan.
verses.translation: And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.

verses.original: Καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν μεγάλην ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ λέγουσαν· Ἄρτι ἐγένετο ἡ σωτηρία καὶ ἡ δύναμις καὶ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν καὶ ἡ ἐξουσία τοῦ χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἐβλήθη ὁ ⸀κατήγωρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἡμῶν, ὁ κατηγορῶν ⸀αὐτοὺς ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός.
verses.translit: Kai ekoysa fonen megalin en to ourano legoysan* Arti egeneto e sotiria kai e dynamis kai e vasileia tou theou emon kai e exoysia tou hristou autou, oti evlithi o katigor ton adelfon emon, o katigoron autous enopion tou theou emon emeras kai nyktos.
verses.translation: And I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night.

verses.original: καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐνίκησαν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸ αἷμα τοῦ ἀρνίου καὶ διὰ τὸν λόγον τῆς μαρτυρίας αὐτῶν, καὶ οὐκ ἠγάπησαν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτῶν ἄχρι θανάτου·
verses.translit: kai autoi enikisan auton dia to aima tou arnioy kai dia ton logon tes martyrias auton, kai ouk egapisan ten psyhen auton ahri thanatoy*
verses.translation: And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.

verses.original: διὰ τοῦτο εὐφραίνεσθε, ⸀οἱ οὐρανοὶ καὶ οἱ ἐν αὐτοῖς σκηνοῦντες. οὐαὶ ⸂τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν⸃, ὅτι κατέβη ὁ διάβολος πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἔχων θυμὸν μέγαν, εἰδὼς ὅτι ὀλίγον καιρὸν ἔχει.
verses.translit: dia touto eufrainesthe, oi ouranoi kai oi en autois skinountes. ouai ten gen kai ten thalassan, oti katevi o diavolos pros umas, ehon thymon megan, eidos oti oligon kairon ehei.
verses.translation: Therefore rejoice, ye heavens, and ye that dwell in them. Woe to the inhabiters of the earth and of the sea! for the devil is come down unto you, having great wrath, because he knoweth that he hath but a short time.

verses.original: Καὶ ὅτε εἶδεν ὁ δράκων ὅτι ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν γῆν, ἐδίωξεν τὴν γυναῖκα ἥτις ἔτεκεν τὸν ἄρσενα.
verses.translit: Kai ote eiden o drakon oti evlithi eis ten gen, edioxen ten gynaika etis eteken ton arsena.
verses.translation: And when the dragon saw that he was cast unto the earth, he persecuted the woman which brought forth the man child .

verses.original: καὶ ἐδόθησαν τῇ γυναικὶ ⸀αἱ δύο πτέρυγες τοῦ ἀετοῦ τοῦ μεγάλου, ἵνα πέτηται εἰς τὴν ἔρημον εἰς τὸν τόπον αὐτῆς, ⸂ὅπου τρέφεται⸃ ἐκεῖ καιρὸν καὶ καιροὺς καὶ ἥμισυ καιροῦ ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ ὄφεως.
verses.translit: kai edothisan te gynaiki ai dyo pteryges tou aetou tou megaloy, ina petitai eis ten erimon eis ton topon autes, opoy trefetai ekei kairon kai kairous kai emisy kairou apo prosopoy tou ofeos.
verses.translation: And to the woman were given two wings of a great eagle, that she might fly into the wilderness, into her place, where she is nourished for a time, and times, and half a time, from the face of the serpent.

verses.original: καὶ ἔβαλεν ὁ ὄφις ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ ὀπίσω τῆς γυναικὸς ὕδωρ ὡς ποταμόν, ἵνα αὐτὴν ποταμοφόρητον ποιήσῃ.
verses.translit: kai evalen o ofis ek tou stomatos autou opiso tes gynaikos udor os potamon, ina auten potamoforiton poiise.
verses.translation: And the serpent cast out of his mouth water as a flood after the woman, that he might cause her to be carried away of the flood.

verses.original: καὶ ἐβοήθησεν ἡ γῆ τῇ γυναικί, καὶ ἤνοιξεν ἡ γῆ τὸ στόμα αὐτῆς καὶ κατέπιεν τὸν ποταμὸν ὃν ἔβαλεν ὁ δράκων ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: kai evoithisen e ge te gynaiki, kai enoixen e ge to stoma autes kai katepien ton potamon on evalen o drakon ek tou stomatos autou*
verses.translation: And the earth helped the woman, and the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed up the flood which the dragon cast out of his mouth.

verses.original: καὶ ὠργίσθη ὁ δράκων ἐπὶ τῇ γυναικί, καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ποιῆσαι πόλεμον μετὰ τῶν λοιπῶν τοῦ σπέρματος αὐτῆς, τῶν τηρούντων τὰς ἐντολὰς τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐχόντων τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ·
verses.translit: kai orgisthi o drakon epi te gynaiki, kai apelthen poiesai polemon meta ton loipon tou spermatos autes, ton tiroynton tas entolas tou theou kai ehonton ten martyrian Iisou*
verses.translation: And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶδον ἐκ τῆς θαλάσσης θηρίον ἀναβαῖνον, ἔχον κέρατα δέκα καὶ κεφαλὰς ἑπτά, καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν κεράτων αὐτοῦ δέκα διαδήματα, καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτοῦ ⸀ὀνόματα βλασφημίας.
verses.translit: Kai eidon ek tes thalassis thirion anavainon, ehon kerata deka kai kefalas epta, kai epi ton keraton autou deka diadimata, kai epi tas kefalas autou onomata vlasfimias.
verses.translation: And I stood upon the sand of the sea, and saw a beast rise up out of the sea, having seven heads and ten horns, and upon his horns ten crowns, and upon his heads the name of blasphemy.

verses.original: καὶ τὸ θηρίον ὃ εἶδον ἦν ὅμοιον παρδάλει, καὶ οἱ πόδες αὐτοῦ ὡς ἄρκου, καὶ τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ ὡς στόμα λέοντος. καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ ὁ δράκων τὴν δύναμιν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξουσίαν μεγάλην.
verses.translit: kai to thirion o eidon en omoion pardalei, kai oi podes autou os arkoy, kai to stoma autou os stoma leontos. kai edoken auto o drakon ten dynamin autou kai ton thronon autou kai exoysian megalin.
verses.translation: And the beast which I saw was like unto a leopard, and his feet were as the feet of a bear, and his mouth as the mouth of a lion: and the dragon gave him his power, and his seat, and great authority.

verses.original: καὶ μίαν ἐκ τῶν κεφαλῶν αὐτοῦ ⸀ὡς ἐσφαγμένην εἰς θάνατον, καὶ ἡ πληγὴ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ ἐθεραπεύθη. καὶ ⸀ἐθαυμάσθη ⸂ὅλη ἡ γῆ⸃ ὀπίσω τοῦ θηρίου,
verses.translit: kai mian ek ton kefalon autou os esfagmenin eis thanaton, kai e plige tou thanatoy autou etherapeythi. kai ethaymasthi oli e ge opiso tou thirioy,
verses.translation: And I saw one of his heads as it were wounded to death; and his deadly wound was healed: and all the world wondered after the beast.

verses.original: καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ δράκοντι ⸂ὅτι ἔδωκεν⸃ τὴν ἐξουσίαν τῷ θηρίῳ, καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ θηρίῳ λέγοντες· Τίς ὅμοιος τῷ θηρίῳ, καὶ τίς ⸀δύναται πολεμῆσαι μετʼ αὐτοῦ;
verses.translit: kai prosekynisan to drakonti oti edoken ten exoysian to thirio, kai prosekynisan to thirio legontes* Tis omoios to thirio, kai tis dynatai polemesai met' autou;
verses.translation: And they worshipped the dragon which gave power unto the beast: and they worshipped the beast, saying, Who is like unto the beast? who is able to make war with him?

verses.original: Καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ στόμα λαλοῦν μεγάλα καὶ ⸀βλασφημίας, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ⸀ἐξουσία ποιῆσαι μῆνας ⸀τεσσεράκοντα δύο.
verses.translit: Kai edothi auto stoma laloun megala kai vlasfimias, kai edothi auto exoysia poiesai menas tesserakonta dyo.
verses.translation: And there was given unto him a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies; and power was given unto him to continue forty and two months.

verses.original: καὶ ἤνοιξε τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ εἰς ⸀βλασφημίας πρὸς τὸν θεόν, βλασφημῆσαι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν σκηνὴν αὐτοῦ, τοὺς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ σκηνοῦντας.
verses.translit: kai enoixe to stoma autou eis vlasfimias pros ton theon, vlasfimesai to onoma autou kai ten skinen autou, tous en to ourano skinountas.
verses.translation: And he opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle, and them that dwell in heaven.

verses.original: καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ποιῆσαι πόλεμον μετὰ τῶν ἁγίων καὶ νικῆσαι αὐτούς, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ἐξουσία ἐπὶ πᾶσαν φυλὴν καὶ λαὸν καὶ γλῶσσαν καὶ ἔθνος.
verses.translit: kai edothi auto poiesai polemon meta ton agion kai nikesai autoys, kai edothi auto exoysia epi pasan fylen kai laon kai glossan kai ethnos.
verses.translation: And it was given unto him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them: and power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations.

verses.original: καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν ⸀αὐτὸν πάντες οἱ κατοικοῦντες ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ⸀οὗ οὐ γέγραπται τὸ ὄνομα ⸀αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τῆς ζωῆς τοῦ ἀρνίου τοῦ ἐσφαγμένου ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου.
verses.translit: kai proskynisoysin auton pantes oi katoikountes epi tes ges, ou ou gegraptai to onoma autou en to vivlio tes zoes tou arnioy tou esfagmenoy apo katavoles kosmoy.
verses.translation: And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.

verses.original: Εἴ τις ἔχει οὖς ἀκουσάτω.
verses.translit: Ei tis ehei ous akoysato.
verses.translation: If any man have an ear, let him hear.

verses.original: εἴ τις ⸂εἰς αἰχμαλωσίαν, εἰς αἰχμαλωσίαν⸃ ὑπάγει· εἴ τις ἐν μαχαίρῃ ⸀ἀποκτανθῆναι αὐτὸν ἐν μαχαίρῃ ἀποκτανθῆναι. ὧδέ ἐστιν ἡ ὑπομονὴ καὶ ἡ πίστις τῶν ἁγίων.
verses.translit: ei tis eis aihmalosian, eis aihmalosian upagei* ei tis en mahaire apoktanthenai auton en mahaire apoktanthenai. ode estin e upomone kai e pistis ton agion.
verses.translation: He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity: he that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλο θηρίον ἀναβαῖνον ἐκ τῆς γῆς, καὶ εἶχεν κέρατα δύο ὅμοια ἀρνίῳ, καὶ ἐλάλει ὡς δράκων.
verses.translit: Kai eidon allo thirion anavainon ek tes ges, kai eihen kerata dyo omoia arnio, kai elalei os drakon.
verses.translation: And I beheld another beast coming up out of the earth; and he had two horns like a lamb, and he spake as a dragon.

verses.original: καὶ τὴν ἐξουσίαν τοῦ πρώτου θηρίου πᾶσαν ποιεῖ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ. καὶ ⸀ποιεῖ τὴν γῆν καὶ τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ κατοικοῦντας ἵνα ⸀προσκυνήσουσιν τὸ θηρίον τὸ πρῶτον, οὗ ἐθεραπεύθη ἡ πληγὴ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai ten exoysian tou protoy thirioy pasan poiei enopion autou. kai poiei ten gen kai tous en aute katoikountas ina proskynisoysin to thirion to proton, ou etherapeythi e plige tou thanatoy autou.
verses.translation: And he exerciseth all the power of the first beast before him, and causeth the earth and them which dwell therein to worship the first beast, whose deadly wound was healed.

verses.original: καὶ ποιεῖ σημεῖα μεγάλα, ⸂ἵνα καὶ πῦρ ποιῇ⸃ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ⸂καταβαίνειν εἰς⸃ τὴν γῆν ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
verses.translit: kai poiei simeia megala, ina kai pur poie ek tou ouranou katavainein eis ten gen enopion ton anthropon.
verses.translation: And he doeth great wonders, so that he maketh fire come down from heaven on the earth in the sight of men,

verses.original: καὶ πλανᾷ ⸀τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς διὰ τὰ σημεῖα ἃ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ποιῆσαι ἐνώπιον τοῦ θηρίου, λέγων τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ποιῆσαι εἰκόνα τῷ θηρίῳ, ⸂ὃς ἔχει⸃ τὴν πληγὴν ⸂τῆς μαχαίρης καὶ ἔζησεν⸃.
verses.translit: kai plana tous katoikountas epi tes ges dia ta simeia a edothi auto poiesai enopion tou thirioy, legon tois katoikousin epi tes ges poiesai eikona to thirio, os ehei ten pligen tes mahairis kai ezisen.
verses.translation: And deceiveth them that dwell on the earth by the means of those miracles which he had power to do in the sight of the beast; saying to them that dwell on the earth, that they should make an image to the beast, which had the wound by a sword, and did live.

verses.original: καὶ ἐδόθη ⸀αὐτῷ ⸂δοῦναι πνεῦμα⸃ τῇ εἰκόνι τοῦ θηρίου, ἵνα καὶ λαλήσῃ ἡ εἰκὼν τοῦ θηρίου καὶ ποιήσῃ ⸀ἵνα ὅσοι ἐὰν μὴ προσκυνήσωσιν τῇ εἰκόνι τοῦ θηρίου ἀποκτανθῶσιν.
verses.translit: kai edothi auto dounai pneuma te eikoni tou thirioy, ina kai lalise e eikon tou thirioy kai poiise ina osoi ean me proskynisosin te eikoni tou thirioy apoktanthosin.
verses.translation: And he had power to give life unto the image of the beast, that the image of the beast should both speak, and cause that as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed.

verses.original: καὶ ποιεῖ πάντας, τοὺς μικροὺς καὶ τοὺς μεγάλους, καὶ τοὺς πλουσίους καὶ τοὺς πτωχούς, καὶ τοὺς ἐλευθέρους καὶ τοὺς δούλους, ἵνα ⸀δῶσιν αὐτοῖς ⸀χάραγμα ἐπὶ τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῶν τῆς δεξιᾶς ἢ ἐπὶ τὸ μέτωπον αὐτῶν,
verses.translit: kai poiei pantas, tous mikrous kai tous megaloys, kai tous ploysioys kai tous ptohoys, kai tous eleytheroys kai tous doyloys, ina dosin autois haragma epi tes heiros auton tes dexias e epi to metopon auton,
verses.translation: And he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads:

verses.original: καὶ ἵνα μή τις ⸀δύνηται ἀγοράσαι ἢ πωλῆσαι εἰ μὴ ὁ ἔχων τὸ χάραγμα, τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ θηρίου ἢ τὸν ἀριθμὸν τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai ina mi tis dynitai agorasai e polesai ei me o ehon to haragma, to onoma tou thirioy e ton arithmon tou onomatos autou.
verses.translation: And that no man might buy or sell, save he that had the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of his name.

verses.original: ὧδε ἡ σοφία ἐστίν· ὁ ἔχων νοῦν ψηφισάτω τὸν ἀριθμὸν τοῦ θηρίου, ἀριθμὸς γὰρ ἀνθρώπου ἐστίν· καὶ ὁ ἀριθμὸς ⸀αὐτοῦ ⸂ἑξακόσιοι ἑξήκοντα ἕξ⸃.
verses.translit: ode e sofia estin* o ehon noun psifisato ton arithmon tou thirioy, arithmos gar anthropoy estin* kai o arithmos autou exakosioi exikonta ex.
verses.translation: Here is wisdom. Let him that hath understanding count the number of the beast: for it is the number of a man; and his number is Six hundred threescore and six.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ τὸ ἀρνίον ⸀ἑστὸς ἐπὶ τὸ ὄρος Σιών, καὶ μετʼ ⸀αὐτοῦ ἑκατὸν τεσσεράκοντα τέσσαρες χιλιάδες ἔχουσαι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένον ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: Kai eidon, kai idou to arnion estos epi to oros Sion, kai met' autou ekaton tesserakonta tessares hiliades ehoysai to onoma autou kai to onoma tou patros autou gegrammenon epi ton metopon auton.
verses.translation: And I looked, and, lo, a Lamb stood on the mount Sion, and with him an hundred forty and four thousand, having his Father’s name written in their foreheads.

verses.original: καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ὡς φωνὴν ὑδάτων πολλῶν καὶ ὡς φωνὴν βροντῆς μεγάλης, καὶ ἡ φωνὴ ἣν ἤκουσα ὡς κιθαρῳδῶν κιθαριζόντων ἐν ταῖς κιθάραις αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai ekoysa fonen ek tou ouranou os fonen udaton pollon kai os fonen vrontes megalis, kai e fone en ekoysa os kitharodon kitharizonton en tais kitharais auton.
verses.translation: And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps:

verses.original: καὶ ᾄδουσιν ⸀ὡς ᾠδὴν καινὴν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου καὶ ἐνώπιον τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων· καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο μαθεῖν τὴν ᾠδὴν εἰ μὴ αἱ ἑκατὸν τεσσεράκοντα τέσσαρες χιλιάδες, οἱ ἠγορασμένοι ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς.
verses.translit: kai adoysin os oden kainen enopion tou thronoy kai enopion ton tessaron zoon kai ton presvyteron* kai oudeis edynato mathein ten oden ei me ai ekaton tesserakonta tessares hiliades, oi egorasmenoi apo tes ges.
verses.translation: And they sung as it were a new song before the throne, and before the four beasts, and the elders: and no man could learn that song but the hundred and forty and four thousand, which were redeemed from the earth.

verses.original: οὗτοί εἰσιν οἳ μετὰ γυναικῶν οὐκ ἐμολύνθησαν, παρθένοι γάρ εἰσιν· ⸀οὗτοι οἱ ἀκολουθοῦντες τῷ ἀρνίῳ ὅπου ἂν ⸀ὑπάγῃ· ⸁οὗτοι ἠγοράσθησαν ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀπαρχὴ τῷ θεῷ καὶ τῷ ἀρνίῳ,
verses.translit: outoi eisin oi meta gynaikon ouk emolynthisan, parthenoi gar eisin* outoi oi akoloythountes to arnio opoy an upage* outoi egorasthisan apo ton anthropon aparhe to theo kai to arnio,
verses.translation: These are they which were not defiled with women; for they are virgins. These are they which follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth. These were redeemed from among men, being the firstfruits unto God and to the Lamb.

verses.original: καὶ ⸂ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτῶν οὐχ εὑρέθη⸃ ψεῦδος· ⸀ἄμωμοί εἰσιν.
verses.translit: kai en to stomati auton ouh eurethi pseudos* amomoi eisin.
verses.translation: And in their mouth was found no guile: for they are without fault before the throne of God.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶδον ⸀ἄλλον ἄγγελον πετόμενον ἐν μεσουρανήματι, ἔχοντα εὐαγγέλιον αἰώνιον εὐαγγελίσαι ⸀ἐπὶ τοὺς καθημένους ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἐπὶ πᾶν ἔθνος καὶ φυλὴν καὶ γλῶσσαν καὶ λαόν,
verses.translit: Kai eidon allon aggelon petomenon en mesoyranimati, ehonta euaggelion aionion euaggelisai epi tous kathimenoys epi tes ges kai epi pan ethnos kai fylen kai glossan kai laon,
verses.translation: And I saw another angel fly in the midst of heaven, having the everlasting gospel to preach unto them that dwell on the earth, and to every nation, and kindred, and tongue, and people,

verses.original: λέγων ἐν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Φοβήθητε τὸν ⸀θεὸν καὶ δότε αὐτῷ δόξαν, ὅτι ἦλθεν ἡ ὥρα τῆς κρίσεως αὐτοῦ, καὶ προσκυνήσατε ⸂τῷ ποιήσαντι⸃ τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν ⸀καὶ θάλασσαν καὶ πηγὰς ὑδάτων.
verses.translit: legon en fone megale* Fovithite ton theon kai dote auto doxan, oti elthen e ora tes kriseos autou, kai proskynisate to poiisanti ton ouranon kai ten gen kai thalassan kai pigas udaton.
verses.translation: Saying with a loud voice, Fear God, and give glory to him; for the hour of his judgment is come: and worship him that made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and the fountains of waters.

verses.original: Καὶ ἄλλος ⸂δεύτερος ἄγγελος⸃ ἠκολούθησεν λέγων· Ἔπεσεν, ⸀ἔπεσεν Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη, ⸀ἣ ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς πεπότικεν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη.
verses.translit: Kai allos deyteros aggelos ekoloythisen legon* Epesen, epesen Vavylon e megali, e ek tou oinoy tou thymou tes porneias autes pepotiken panta ta ethni.
verses.translation: And there followed another angel, saying, Babylon is fallen, is fallen, that great city, because she made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication.

verses.original: Καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος τρίτος ἠκολούθησεν αὐτοῖς λέγων ἐν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Εἴ τις προσκυνεῖ τὸ θηρίον καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα αὐτοῦ, καὶ λαμβάνει χάραγμα ἐπὶ τοῦ μετώπου αὐτοῦ ἢ ἐπὶ τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: Kai allos aggelos tritos ekoloythisen autois legon en fone megale* Ei tis proskynei to thirion kai ten eikona autou, kai lamvanei haragma epi tou metopoy autou e epi ten heira autou,
verses.translation: And the third angel followed them, saying with a loud voice, If any man worship the beast and his image, and receive his mark in his forehead, or in his hand,

verses.original: καὶ αὐτὸς πίεται ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ κεκερασμένου ἀκράτου ἐν τῷ ποτηρίῳ τῆς ὀργῆς αὐτοῦ, καὶ βασανισθήσεται ἐν πυρὶ καὶ θείῳ ἐνώπιον ⸂ἀγγέλων ἁγίων⸃ καὶ ἐνώπιον τοῦ ἀρνίου.
verses.translit: kai autos pietai ek tou oinoy tou thymou tou theou tou kekerasmenoy akratoy en to potirio tes orges autou, kai vasanisthisetai en pyri kai theio enopion aggelon agion kai enopion tou arnioy.
verses.translation: The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb:

verses.original: καὶ ὁ καπνὸς τοῦ βασανισμοῦ αὐτῶν εἰς αἰῶνας αἰώνων ἀναβαίνει, καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἀνάπαυσιν ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός, οἱ προσκυνοῦντες τὸ θηρίον καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα αὐτοῦ, καὶ εἴ τις λαμβάνει τὸ χάραγμα τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai o kapnos tou vasanismou auton eis aionas aionon anavainei, kai ouk ehoysin anapaysin emeras kai nyktos, oi proskynountes to thirion kai ten eikona autou, kai ei tis lamvanei to haragma tou onomatos autou.
verses.translation: And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: and they have no rest day nor night, who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name.

verses.original: Ὧδε ἡ ὑπομονὴ τῶν ἁγίων ἐστίν, οἱ τηροῦντες τὰς ἐντολὰς τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τὴν πίστιν Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: Ode e upomone ton agion estin, oi tirountes tas entolas tou theou kai ten pistin Iisou.
verses.translation: Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.

verses.original: Καὶ ἤκουσα φωνῆς ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ λεγούσης· Γράψον· Μακάριοι οἱ νεκροὶ οἱ ἐν κυρίῳ ἀποθνῄσκοντες ἀπʼ ἄρτι. ⸂ναί, λέγει⸃ τὸ πνεῦμα, ἵνα ⸀ἀναπαήσονται ἐκ τῶν κόπων αὐτῶν, τὰ ⸀γὰρ ἔργα αὐτῶν ἀκολουθεῖ μετʼ αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: Kai ekoysa fones ek tou ouranou legoysis* Grapson* Makarioi oi nekroi oi en kyrio apothneskontes ap' arti. nai, legei to pneuma, ina anapaisontai ek ton kopon auton, ta gar erga auton akoloythei met' auton.
verses.translation: And I heard a voice from heaven saying unto me, Write, Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord from henceforth: Yea, saith the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ νεφέλη λευκή, καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν νεφέλην καθήμενον ὅμοιον ⸀υἱὸν ἀνθρώπου, ἔχων ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ στέφανον χρυσοῦν καὶ ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ δρέπανον ὀξύ.
verses.translit: Kai eidon, kai idou nefeli leyki, kai epi ten nefelin kathimenon omoion yion anthropoy, ehon epi tes kefales autou stefanon hrysoun kai en te heiri autou drepanon oxy.
verses.translation: And I looked, and behold a white cloud, and upon the cloud one sat like unto the Son of man, having on his head a golden crown, and in his hand a sharp sickle.

verses.original: καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ κράζων ἐν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ τῆς νεφέλης· Πέμψον τὸ δρέπανόν σου καὶ θέρισον, ὅτι ἦλθεν ἡ ὥρα θερίσαι, ὅτι ἐξηράνθη ὁ θερισμὸς τῆς γῆς.
verses.translit: kai allos aggelos exelthen ek tou naou krazon en fone megale to kathimeno epi tes nefelis* Pempson to drepanon soy kai therison, oti elthen e ora therisai, oti exiranthi o therismos tes ges.
verses.translation: And another angel came out of the temple, crying with a loud voice to him that sat on the cloud, Thrust in thy sickle, and reap: for the time is come for thee to reap; for the harvest of the earth is ripe.

verses.original: καὶ ἔβαλεν ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ ⸂τῆς νεφέλης⸃ τὸ δρέπανον αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν, καὶ ἐθερίσθη ἡ γῆ.
verses.translit: kai evalen o kathimenos epi tes nefelis to drepanon autou epi ten gen, kai etheristhi e ge.
verses.translation: And he that sat on the cloud thrust in his sickle on the earth; and the earth was reaped.

verses.original: Καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ τοῦ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ἔχων καὶ αὐτὸς δρέπανον ὀξύ.
verses.translit: Kai allos aggelos exelthen ek tou naou tou en to ourano, ehon kai autos drepanon oxy.
verses.translation: And another angel came out of the temple which is in heaven, he also having a sharp sickle.

verses.original: καὶ ἄλλος ⸀ἄγγελος ἐκ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, ⸀ὁ ἔχων ἐξουσίαν ἐπὶ τοῦ πυρός, καὶ ἐφώνησεν ⸀φωνῇ μεγάλῃ τῷ ἔχοντι τὸ δρέπανον τὸ ὀξὺ λέγων· Πέμψον σου τὸ δρέπανον τὸ ὀξὺ καὶ τρύγησον τοὺς βότρυας τῆς ἀμπέλου τῆς γῆς, ὅτι ἤκμασαν αἱ σταφυλαὶ αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: kai allos aggelos ek tou thysiastirioy, o ehon exoysian epi tou pyros, kai efonisen fone megale to ehonti to drepanon to oxu legon* Pempson soy to drepanon to oxu kai trygison tous votryas tes ampeloy tes ges, oti ekmasan ai stafylai autes.
verses.translation: And another angel came out from the altar, which had power over fire; and cried with a loud cry to him that had the sharp sickle, saying, Thrust in thy sharp sickle, and gather the clusters of the vine of the earth; for her grapes are fully ripe.

verses.original: καὶ ἔβαλεν ὁ ἄγγελος τὸ δρέπανον αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν γῆν, καὶ ἐτρύγησεν τὴν ἄμπελον τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἔβαλεν εἰς τὴν ληνὸν τοῦ θυμοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ τὸν μέγαν.
verses.translit: kai evalen o aggelos to drepanon autou eis ten gen, kai etrygisen ten ampelon tes ges, kai evalen eis ten linon tou thymou tou theou ton megan.
verses.translation: And the angel thrust in his sickle into the earth, and gathered the vine of the earth, and cast it into the great winepress of the wrath of God.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπατήθη ἡ ληνὸς ἔξωθεν τῆς πόλεως, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν αἷμα ἐκ τῆς ληνοῦ ἄχρι τῶν χαλινῶν τῶν ἵππων ἀπὸ σταδίων χιλίων ἑξακοσίων.
verses.translit: kai epatithi e linos exothen tes poleos, kai exelthen aima ek tes linou ahri ton halinon ton ippon apo stadion hilion exakosion.
verses.translation: And the winepress was trodden without the city, and blood came out of the winepress, even unto the horse bridles, by the space of a thousand and six hundred furlongs.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλο σημεῖον ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ μέγα καὶ θαυμαστόν, ἀγγέλους ἑπτὰ ἔχοντας πληγὰς ἑπτὰ τὰς ἐσχάτας, ὅτι ἐν αὐταῖς ἐτελέσθη ὁ θυμὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: Kai eidon allo simeion en to ourano mega kai thaymaston, aggeloys epta ehontas pligas epta tas eshatas, oti en autais etelesthi o thymos tou theou.
verses.translation: And I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvellous, seven angels having the seven last plagues; for in them is filled up the wrath of God.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶδον ὡς θάλασσαν ὑαλίνην μεμιγμένην πυρί, καὶ τοὺς νικῶντας ἐκ τοῦ θηρίου καὶ ἐκ τῆς εἰκόνος αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκ τοῦ ἀριθμοῦ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ ἑστῶτας ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν τὴν ὑαλίνην, ἔχοντας κιθάρας τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: Kai eidon os thalassan ualinin memigmenin pyri, kai tous nikontas ek tou thirioy kai ek tes eikonos autou kai ek tou arithmou tou onomatos autou estotas epi ten thalassan ten ualinin, ehontas kitharas tou theou.
verses.translation: And I saw as it were a sea of glass mingled with fire: and them that had gotten the victory over the beast, and over his image, and over his mark, and over the number of his name, stand on the sea of glass, having the harps of God.

verses.original: καὶ ᾄδουσιν τὴν ᾠδὴν Μωϋσέως τοῦ δούλου τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τὴν ᾠδὴν τοῦ ἀρνίου λέγοντες· Μεγάλα καὶ θαυμαστὰ τὰ ἔργα σου, κύριε, ὁ θεός, ὁ παντοκράτωρ· δίκαιαι καὶ ἀληθιναὶ αἱ ὁδοί σου, ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν ⸀αἰώνων·
verses.translit: kai adoysin ten oden Moyseos tou doyloy tou theou kai ten oden tou arnioy legontes* Megala kai thaymasta ta erga soy, kyrie, o theos, o pantokrator* dikaiai kai alithinai ai odoi soy, o vasileus ton aionon*
verses.translation: And they sing the song of Moses the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying, Great and marvellous are thy works, Lord God Almighty; just and true are thy ways, thou King of saints.

verses.original: τίς οὐ μὴ ⸀φοβηθῇ, κύριε, καὶ ⸀δοξάσει τὸ ὄνομά σου, ὅτι μόνος ⸀ὅσιος; ὅτι πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἥξουσιν καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν ἐνώπιόν σου, ὅτι τὰ δικαιώματά σου ἐφανερώθησαν.
verses.translit: tis ou me fovithe, kyrie, kai doxasei to onoma soy, oti monos osios? oti panta ta ethni exoysin kai proskynisoysin enopion soy, oti ta dikaiomata soy efanerothisan.
verses.translation: Who shall not fear thee, O Lord, and glorify thy name? for thou only art holy: for all nations shall come and worship before thee; for thy judgments are made manifest.

verses.original: Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα εἶδον, καὶ ἠνοίγη ὁ ναὸς τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ,
verses.translit: Kai meta tauta eidon, kai enoigi o naos tes skines tou martyrioy en to ourano,
verses.translation: And after that I looked, and, behold, the temple of the tabernacle of the testimony in heaven was opened:

verses.original: καὶ ἐξῆλθον οἱ ἑπτὰ ἄγγελοι οἱ ἔχοντες τὰς ἑπτὰ πληγὰς ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ, ⸀ἐνδεδυμένοι ⸀λίνον καθαρὸν λαμπρὸν καὶ περιεζωσμένοι περὶ τὰ στήθη ζώνας χρυσᾶς.
verses.translit: kai exelthon oi epta aggeloi oi ehontes tas epta pligas ek tou naou, endedymenoi linon katharon lampron kai periezosmenoi peri ta stithi zonas hrysas.
verses.translation: And the seven angels came out of the temple, having the seven plagues, clothed in pure and white linen, and having their breasts girded with golden girdles.

verses.original: καὶ ἓν ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων ἔδωκεν τοῖς ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλοις ἑπτὰ φιάλας χρυσᾶς γεμούσας τοῦ θυμοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων.
verses.translit: kai en ek ton tessaron zoon edoken tois epta aggelois epta fialas hrysas gemoysas tou thymou tou theou tou zontos eis tous aionas ton aionon.
verses.translation: And one of the four beasts gave unto the seven angels seven golden vials full of the wrath of God, who liveth for ever and ever.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγεμίσθη ὁ ναὸς καπνοῦ ἐκ τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐκ τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὸν ναὸν ἄχρι τελεσθῶσιν αἱ ἑπτὰ πληγαὶ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλων.
verses.translit: kai egemisthi o naos kapnou ek tes doxis tou theou kai ek tes dynameos autou, kai oudeis edynato eiselthein eis ton naon ahri telesthosin ai epta pligai ton epta aggelon.
verses.translation: And the temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God, and from his power; and no man was able to enter into the temple, till the seven plagues of the seven angels were fulfilled.

verses.original: Καὶ ἤκουσα ⸂μεγάλης φωνῆς⸃ ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ λεγούσης τοῖς ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλοις· Ὑπάγετε καὶ ⸀ἐκχέετε τὰς ἑπτὰ φιάλας τοῦ θυμοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς τὴν γῆν.
verses.translit: Kai ekoysa megalis fones ek tou naou legoysis tois epta aggelois* Upagete kai ekheete tas epta fialas tou thymou tou theou eis ten gen.
verses.translation: And I heard a great voice out of the temple saying to the seven angels, Go your ways, and pour out the vials of the wrath of God upon the earth.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ὁ πρῶτος καὶ ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν γῆν· καὶ ἐγένετο ἕλκος κακὸν καὶ πονηρὸν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τοὺς ἔχοντας τὸ χάραγμα τοῦ θηρίου καὶ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας τῇ εἰκόνι αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Kai apelthen o protos kai exeheen ten fialin autou eis ten gen* kai egeneto elkos kakon kai poniron epi tous anthropoys tous ehontas to haragma tou thirioy kai tous proskynountas te eikoni autou.
verses.translation: And the first went, and poured out his vial upon the earth; and there fell a noisome and grievous sore upon the men which had the mark of the beast, and upon them which worshipped his image.

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ ⸀δεύτερος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν· καὶ ἐγένετο αἷμα ὡς νεκροῦ, καὶ πᾶσα ψυχὴ ⸀ζωῆς ἀπέθανεν ⸀τὰ ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ.
verses.translit: Kai o deyteros exeheen ten fialin autou eis ten thalassan* kai egeneto aima os nekrou, kai pasa psyhe zoes apethanen ta en te thalasse.
verses.translation: And the second angel poured out his vial upon the sea; and it became as the blood of a dead man : and every living soul died in the sea.

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ τρίτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς ποταμοὺς ⸀καὶ τὰς πηγὰς τῶν ὑδάτων· καὶ ἐγένετο αἷμα.
verses.translit: Kai o tritos exeheen ten fialin autou eis tous potamous kai tas pigas ton udaton* kai egeneto aima.
verses.translation: And the third angel poured out his vial upon the rivers and fountains of waters; and they became blood.

verses.original: καὶ ἤκουσα τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῶν ὑδάτων λέγοντος· Δίκαιος εἶ, ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν, ⸀ὁ ὅσιος, ὅτι ταῦτα ἔκρινας,
verses.translit: kai ekoysa tou aggeloy ton udaton legontos* Dikaios ei, o on kai o en, o osios, oti tauta ekrinas,
verses.translation: And I heard the angel of the waters say, Thou art righteous, O Lord, which art, and wast, and shalt be, because thou hast judged thus.

verses.original: ὅτι αἷμα ἁγίων καὶ προφητῶν ἐξέχεαν, καὶ αἷμα αὐτοῖς ⸀δέδωκας πιεῖν· ἄξιοί εἰσιν.
verses.translit: oti aima agion kai profiton exehean, kai aima autois dedokas piein* axioi eisin.
verses.translation: For they have shed the blood of saints and prophets, and thou hast given them blood to drink; for they are worthy.

verses.original: καὶ ἤκουσα τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου λέγοντος· Ναί, κύριε, ὁ θεός, ὁ παντοκράτωρ, ἀληθιναὶ καὶ δίκαιαι αἱ κρίσεις σου.
verses.translit: kai ekoysa tou thysiastirioy legontos* Nai, kyrie, o theos, o pantokrator, alithinai kai dikaiai ai kriseis soy.
verses.translation: And I heard another out of the altar say, Even so, Lord God Almighty, true and righteous are thy judgments.

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ ⸀τέταρτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν ἥλιον· καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ καυματίσαι ⸂τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἐν πυρί⸃.
verses.translit: Kai o tetartos exeheen ten fialin autou epi ton elion* kai edothi auto kaymatisai tous anthropoys en pyri.
verses.translation: And the fourth angel poured out his vial upon the sun; and power was given unto him to scorch men with fire.

verses.original: καὶ ἐκαυματίσθησαν οἱ ἄνθρωποι καῦμα μέγα· καὶ ⸀ἐβλασφήμησαν τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ἔχοντος ⸀τὴν ἐξουσίαν ἐπὶ τὰς πληγὰς ταύτας, καὶ οὐ μετενόησαν δοῦναι αὐτῷ δόξαν.
verses.translit: kai ekaymatisthisan oi anthropoi kauma mega* kai evlasfimisan to onoma tou theou tou ehontos ten exoysian epi tas pligas taytas, kai ou metenoisan dounai auto doxan.
verses.translation: And men were scorched with great heat, and blasphemed the name of God, which hath power over these plagues: and they repented not to give him glory.

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ πέμπτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν θρόνον τοῦ θηρίου· καὶ ἐγένετο ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ ἐσκοτωμένη, καὶ ἐμασῶντο τὰς γλώσσας αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ πόνου,
verses.translit: Kai o pemptos exeheen ten fialin autou epi ton thronon tou thirioy* kai egeneto e vasileia autou eskotomeni, kai emasonto tas glossas auton ek tou ponoy,
verses.translation: And the fifth angel poured out his vial upon the seat of the beast; and his kingdom was full of darkness; and they gnawed their tongues for pain,

verses.original: καὶ ἐβλασφήμησαν τὸν θεὸν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐκ τῶν πόνων αὐτῶν καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἑλκῶν αὐτῶν, καὶ οὐ μετενόησαν ἐκ τῶν ἔργων αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai evlasfimisan ton theon tou ouranou ek ton ponon auton kai ek ton elkon auton, kai ou metenoisan ek ton ergon auton.
verses.translation: And blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their sores, and repented not of their deeds.

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ ἕκτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν ποταμὸν τὸν μέγαν ⸀τὸν Εὐφράτην· καὶ ἐξηράνθη τὸ ὕδωρ αὐτοῦ, ἵνα ἑτοιμασθῇ ἡ ὁδὸς τῶν βασιλέων τῶν ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς ἡλίου.
verses.translit: Kai o ektos exeheen ten fialin autou epi ton potamon ton megan ton Eufratin* kai exiranthi to udor autou, ina etoimasthe e odos ton vasileon ton apo anatoles elioy.
verses.translation: And the sixth angel poured out his vial upon the great river Euphrates; and the water thereof was dried up, that the way of the kings of the east might be prepared.

verses.original: καὶ εἶδον ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ δράκοντος καὶ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ θηρίου καὶ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ ψευδοπροφήτου πνεύματα ⸂τρία ἀκάθαρτα⸃ ὡς βάτραχοι·
verses.translit: kai eidon ek tou stomatos tou drakontos kai ek tou stomatos tou thirioy kai ek tou stomatos tou pseydoprofitoy pneymata tria akatharta os vatrahoi*
verses.translation: And I saw three unclean spirits like frogs come out of the mouth of the dragon, and out of the mouth of the beast, and out of the mouth of the false prophet.

verses.original: εἰσὶν γὰρ πνεύματα δαιμονίων ποιοῦντα σημεῖα, ἃ ἐκπορεύεται ἐπὶ τοὺς βασιλεῖς τῆς οἰκουμένης ὅλης, συναγαγεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν πόλεμον τῆς ⸀ἡμέρας τῆς μεγάλης τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ παντοκράτορος—
verses.translit: eisin gar pneymata daimonion poiounta simeia, a ekporeyetai epi tous vasileis tes oikoymenis olis, synagagein autous eis ton polemon tes emeras tes megalis tou theou tou pantokratoros--
verses.translation: For they are the spirits of devils, working miracles, which go forth unto the kings of the earth and of the whole world, to gather them to the battle of that great day of God Almighty.

verses.original: Ἰδοὺ ἔρχομαι ὡς κλέπτης. μακάριος ὁ γρηγορῶν καὶ τηρῶν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ, ἵνα μὴ γυμνὸς περιπατῇ καὶ βλέπωσιν τὴν ἀσχημοσύνην αὐτοῦ—
verses.translit: Idou erhomai os kleptis. makarios o grigoron kai tiron ta imatia autou, ina me gymnos peripate kai vleposin ten ashimosynin autou--
verses.translation: Behold, I come as a thief. Blessed is he that watcheth, and keepeth his garments, lest he walk naked, and they see his shame.

verses.original: καὶ συνήγαγεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν τόπον τὸν καλούμενον Ἑβραϊστὶ Ἁρμαγεδών.
verses.translit: kai synigagen autous eis ton topon ton kaloymenon Evraisti Armagedon.
verses.translation: And he gathered them together into a place called in the Hebrew tongue Armageddon.

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ ἕβδομος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν ἀέρα— καὶ ἐξῆλθεν φωνὴ μεγάλη ⸀ἐκ τοῦ ⸀ναοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ θρόνου λέγουσα· Γέγονεν—
verses.translit: Kai o evdomos exeheen ten fialin autou epi ton aera-- kai exelthen fone megali ek tou naou apo tou thronoy legoysa* Gegonen--
verses.translation: And the seventh angel poured out his vial into the air; and there came a great voice out of the temple of heaven, from the throne, saying, It is done.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγένοντο ἀστραπαὶ καὶ ⸂φωναὶ καὶ βρονταί⸃, καὶ σεισμὸς ⸀ἐγένετο μέγας, οἷος οὐκ ἐγένετο ἀφʼ οὗ ⸂ἄνθρωποι ἐγένοντο⸃ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς τηλικοῦτος σεισμὸς οὕτω μέγας,
verses.translit: kai egenonto astrapai kai fonai kai vrontai, kai seismos egeneto megas, oios ouk egeneto af' ou anthropoi egenonto epi tes ges tilikoutos seismos outo megas,
verses.translation: And there were voices, and thunders, and lightnings; and there was a great earthquake, such as was not since men were upon the earth, so mighty an earthquake, and so great.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη εἰς τρία μέρη, καὶ αἱ πόλεις τῶν ἐθνῶν ἔπεσαν· καὶ Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη ἐμνήσθη ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ δοῦναι αὐτῇ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τῆς ὀργῆς αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: kai egeneto e polis e megali eis tria meri, kai ai poleis ton ethnon epesan* kai Vavylon e megali emnisthi enopion tou theou dounai aute to potirion tou oinoy tou thymou tes orges autou*
verses.translation: And the great city was divided into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell: and great Babylon came in remembrance before God, to give unto her the cup of the wine of the fierceness of his wrath.

verses.original: καὶ πᾶσα νῆσος ἔφυγεν, καὶ ὄρη οὐχ εὑρέθησαν.
verses.translit: kai pasa nesos efygen, kai ori ouh eurethisan.
verses.translation: And every island fled away, and the mountains were not found.

verses.original: καὶ χάλαζα μεγάλη ὡς ταλαντιαία καταβαίνει ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους· καὶ ἐβλασφήμησαν οἱ ἄνθρωποι τὸν θεὸν ἐκ τῆς πληγῆς τῆς χαλάζης, ὅτι μεγάλη ἐστὶν ἡ πληγὴ αὐτῆς σφόδρα.
verses.translit: kai halaza megali os talantiaia katavainei ek tou ouranou epi tous anthropoys* kai evlasfimisan oi anthropoi ton theon ek tes pliges tes halazis, oti megali estin e plige autes sfodra.
verses.translation: And there fell upon men a great hail out of heaven, every stone about the weight of a talent: and men blasphemed God because of the plague of the hail; for the plague thereof was exceeding great.

verses.original: Καὶ ἦλθεν εἷς ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλων τῶν ἐχόντων τὰς ἑπτὰ φιάλας, καὶ ἐλάλησεν μετʼ ἐμοῦ λέγων· Δεῦρο, δείξω σοι τὸ κρίμα τῆς πόρνης τῆς μεγάλης τῆς καθημένης ἐπὶ ⸀ὑδάτων πολλῶν,
verses.translit: Kai elthen eis ek ton epta aggelon ton ehonton tas epta fialas, kai elalisen met' emou legon* Deuro, deixo soi to krima tes pornis tes megalis tes kathimenis epi udaton pollon,
verses.translation: And there came one of the seven angels which had the seven vials, and talked with me, saying unto me, Come hither; I will shew unto thee the judgment of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters:
