verses.original: μεθʼ ἧς ἐπόρνευσαν οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἐμεθύσθησαν οἱ κατοικοῦντες τὴν γῆν ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: meth' es eporneysan oi vasileis tes ges, kai emethysthisan oi katoikountes ten gen ek tou oinoy tes porneias autes.
verses.translation: With whom the kings of the earth have committed fornication, and the inhabitants of the earth have been made drunk with the wine of her fornication.

verses.original: καὶ ἀπήνεγκέν με εἰς ἔρημον ἐν πνεύματι. καὶ εἶδον γυναῖκα καθημένην ἐπὶ θηρίον κόκκινον, ⸀γέμοντα ὀνόματα βλασφημίας, ⸀ἔχων κεφαλὰς ἑπτὰ καὶ κέρατα δέκα.
verses.translit: kai apinegken me eis erimon en pneymati. kai eidon gynaika kathimenin epi thirion kokkinon, gemonta onomata vlasfimias, ehon kefalas epta kai kerata deka.
verses.translation: So he carried me away in the spirit into the wilderness: and I saw a woman sit upon a scarlet coloured beast, full of names of blasphemy, having seven heads and ten horns.

verses.original: καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἦν περιβεβλημένη πορφυροῦν καὶ κόκκινον, ⸀καὶ κεχρυσωμένη ⸀χρυσίῳ καὶ λίθῳ τιμίῳ καὶ μαργαρίταις, ἔχουσα ποτήριον χρυσοῦν ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτῆς γέμον βδελυγμάτων καὶ τὰ ἀκάθαρτα τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς,
verses.translit: kai e gyne en perivevlimeni porfyroun kai kokkinon, kai kehrysomeni hrysio kai litho timio kai margaritais, ehoysa potirion hrysoun en te heiri autes gemon vdelygmaton kai ta akatharta tes porneias autes,
verses.translation: And the woman was arrayed in purple and scarlet colour, and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls, having a golden cup in her hand full of abominations and filthiness of her fornication:

verses.original: καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ μέτωπον αὐτῆς ὄνομα γεγραμμένον, μυστήριον, Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη, ἡ μήτηρ τῶν πορνῶν καὶ τῶν βδελυγμάτων τῆς γῆς.
verses.translit: kai epi to metopon autes onoma gegrammenon, mystirion, Vavylon e megali, e mitir ton pornon kai ton vdelygmaton tes ges.
verses.translation: And upon her forehead was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.

verses.original: καὶ εἶδον τὴν γυναῖκα μεθύουσαν ἐκ τοῦ αἵματος τῶν ἁγίων ⸀καὶ ἐκ τοῦ αἵματος τῶν μαρτύρων Ἰησοῦ. Καὶ ἐθαύμασα ἰδὼν αὐτὴν θαῦμα μέγα·
verses.translit: kai eidon ten gynaika methyoysan ek tou aimatos ton agion kai ek tou aimatos ton martyron Iisou. Kai ethaymasa idon auten thauma mega*
verses.translation: And I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus: and when I saw her, I wondered with great admiration.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπέν μοι ὁ ἄγγελος· Διὰ τί ἐθαύμασας; ἐγὼ ἐρῶ σοι τὸ μυστήριον τῆς γυναικὸς καὶ τοῦ θηρίου τοῦ βαστάζοντος αὐτήν, τοῦ ἔχοντος τὰς ἑπτὰ κεφαλὰς καὶ τὰ δέκα κέρατα·
verses.translit: kai eipen moi o aggelos* Dia ti ethaymasas; ego ero soi to mystirion tes gynaikos kai tou thirioy tou vastazontos autin, tou ehontos tas epta kefalas kai ta deka kerata*
verses.translation: And the angel said unto me, Wherefore didst thou marvel? I will tell thee the mystery of the woman, and of the beast that carrieth her, which hath the seven heads and ten horns.

verses.original: τὸ θηρίον ὃ εἶδες ἦν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν, καὶ μέλλει ἀναβαίνειν ἐκ τῆς ἀβύσσου, καὶ εἰς ἀπώλειαν ⸀ὑπάγει· καὶ ⸀θαυμασθήσονται οἱ κατοικοῦντες ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὧν οὐ γέγραπται ⸂τὸ ὄνομα⸃ ἐπὶ τὸ βιβλίον τῆς ζωῆς ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου, βλεπόντων ⸂τὸ θηρίον ὅτι ἦν⸃ καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν καὶ παρέσται.
verses.translit: to thirion o eides en kai ouk estin, kai mellei anavainein ek tes avyssoy, kai eis apoleian upagei* kai thaymasthisontai oi katoikountes epi tes ges, on ou gegraptai to onoma epi to vivlion tes zoes apo katavoles kosmoy, vleponton to thirion oti en kai ouk estin kai parestai.
verses.translation: The beast that thou sawest was, and is not; and shall ascend out of the bottomless pit, and go into perdition: and they that dwell on the earth shall wonder, whose names were not written in the book of life from the foundation of the world, when they behold the beast that was, and is not, and yet is.

verses.original: Ὧδε ὁ νοῦς ὁ ἔχων σοφίαν. αἱ ἑπτὰ κεφαλαὶ ἑπτὰ ὄρη εἰσίν, ὅπου ἡ γυνὴ κάθηται ἐπʼ αὐτῶν. καὶ βασιλεῖς ⸂ἑπτά εἰσιν⸃·
verses.translit: Ode o nous o ehon sofian. ai epta kefalai epta ori eisin, opoy e gyne kathitai ep' auton. kai vasileis epta eisin*
verses.translation: And here is the mind which hath wisdom. The seven heads are seven mountains, on which the woman sitteth.

verses.original: οἱ πέντε ἔπεσαν, ὁ εἷς ἔστιν, ὁ ἄλλος οὔπω ἦλθεν, καὶ ὅταν ἔλθῃ ὀλίγον ⸂αὐτὸν δεῖ⸃ μεῖναι,
verses.translit: oi pente epesan, o eis estin, o allos oupo elthen, kai otan elthe oligon auton dei meinai,
verses.translation: And there are seven kings: five are fallen, and one is, and the other is not yet come; and when he cometh, he must continue a short space.

verses.original: καὶ τὸ θηρίον ὃ ἦν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν. καὶ ⸀αὐτὸς ὄγδοός ἐστιν καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἑπτά ἐστιν, καὶ εἰς ἀπώλειαν ὑπάγει.
verses.translit: kai to thirion o en kai ouk estin. kai autos ogdoos estin kai ek ton epta estin, kai eis apoleian upagei.
verses.translation: And the beast that was, and is not, even he is the eighth, and is of the seven, and goeth into perdition.

verses.original: καὶ τὰ δέκα κέρατα ἃ εἶδες δέκα βασιλεῖς εἰσιν, οἵτινες βασιλείαν οὔπω ἔλαβον, ἀλλὰ ἐξουσίαν ὡς βασιλεῖς μίαν ὥραν λαμβάνουσιν μετὰ τοῦ θηρίου.
verses.translit: kai ta deka kerata a eides deka vasileis eisin, oitines vasileian oupo elavon, alla exoysian os vasileis mian oran lamvanoysin meta tou thirioy.
verses.translation: And the ten horns which thou sawest are ten kings, which have received no kingdom as yet; but receive power as kings one hour with the beast.

verses.original: οὗτοι μίαν ⸂γνώμην ἔχουσιν⸃, καὶ τὴν δύναμιν ⸀καὶ ἐξουσίαν αὐτῶν τῷ θηρίῳ διδόασιν.
verses.translit: outoi mian gnomin ehoysin, kai ten dynamin kai exoysian auton to thirio didoasin.
verses.translation: These have one mind, and shall give their power and strength unto the beast.

verses.original: οὗτοι μετὰ τοῦ ἀρνίου πολεμήσουσιν, καὶ τὸ ἀρνίον νικήσει αὐτούς, ὅτι κύριος κυρίων ἐστὶν καὶ βασιλεὺς βασιλέων, καὶ οἱ μετʼ αὐτοῦ κλητοὶ καὶ ἐκλεκτοὶ καὶ πιστοί.
verses.translit: outoi meta tou arnioy polemisoysin, kai to arnion nikisei autoys, oti kyrios kyrion estin kai vasileus vasileon, kai oi met' autou klitoi kai eklektoi kai pistoi.
verses.translation: These shall make war with the Lamb, and the Lamb shall overcome them: for he is Lord of lords, and King of kings: and they that are with him are called, and chosen, and faithful.

verses.original: Καὶ λέγει μοι· Τὰ ὕδατα ἃ εἶδες, οὗ ἡ πόρνη κάθηται, λαοὶ καὶ ὄχλοι εἰσὶν καὶ ἔθνη καὶ γλῶσσαι.
verses.translit: Kai legei moi* Ta udata a eides, ou e porni kathitai, laoi kai ohloi eisin kai ethni kai glossai.
verses.translation: And he saith unto me, The waters which thou sawest, where the whore sitteth, are peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues.

verses.original: καὶ τὰ δέκα κέρατα ἃ εἶδες καὶ τὸ θηρίον, οὗτοι μισήσουσι τὴν πόρνην, καὶ ἠρημωμένην ποιήσουσιν αὐτὴν καὶ ⸀γυμνήν, καὶ τὰς σάρκας αὐτῆς φάγονται, καὶ αὐτὴν κατακαύσουσιν ἐν πυρί·
verses.translit: kai ta deka kerata a eides kai to thirion, outoi misisoysi ten pornin, kai erimomenin poiisoysin auten kai gymnin, kai tas sarkas autes fagontai, kai auten katakaysoysin en pyri*
verses.translation: And the ten horns which thou sawest upon the beast, these shall hate the whore, and shall make her desolate and naked, and shall eat her flesh, and burn her with fire.

verses.original: ὁ γὰρ θεὸς ἔδωκεν εἰς τὰς καρδίας αὐτῶν ποιῆσαι τὴν γνώμην αὐτοῦ, καὶ ποιῆσαι ⸂μίαν γνώμην⸃ καὶ δοῦναι τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτῶν τῷ θηρίῳ, ἄχρι ⸀τελεσθήσονται οἱ λόγοι τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: o gar theos edoken eis tas kardias auton poiesai ten gnomin autou, kai poiesai mian gnomin kai dounai ten vasileian auton to thirio, ahri telesthisontai oi logoi tou theou.
verses.translation: For God hath put in their hearts to fulfil his will, and to agree, and give their kingdom unto the beast, until the words of God shall be fulfilled.

verses.original: καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἣν εἶδες ἔστιν ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη ἡ ἔχουσα βασιλείαν ἐπὶ τῶν βασιλέων τῆς γῆς.
verses.translit: kai e gyne en eides estin e polis e megali e ehoysa vasileian epi ton vasileon tes ges.
verses.translation: And the woman which thou sawest is that great city, which reigneth over the kings of the earth.

verses.original: Μετὰ ταῦτα εἶδον ἄλλον ἄγγελον καταβαίνοντα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ἔχοντα ἐξουσίαν μεγάλην, καὶ ἡ γῆ ἐφωτίσθη ἐκ τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Meta tauta eidon allon aggelon katavainonta ek tou ouranou, ehonta exoysian megalin, kai e ge efotisthi ek tes doxis autou.
verses.translation: And after these things I saw another angel come down from heaven, having great power; and the earth was lightened with his glory.

verses.original: καὶ ἔκραξεν ⸀ἐν ἰσχυρᾷ φωνῇ λέγων· Ἔπεσεν, ⸀ἔπεσεν Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη, καὶ ἐγένετο κατοικητήριον ⸀δαιμονίων καὶ φυλακὴ παντὸς πνεύματος ἀκαθάρτου καὶ φυλακὴ παντὸς ὀρνέου ἀκαθάρτου ⸂καὶ φυλακὴ παντὸς θηρίου ἀκαθάρτου⸃ καὶ μεμισημένου,
verses.translit: kai ekraxen en ishyra fone legon* Epesen, epesen Vavylon e megali, kai egeneto katoikitirion daimonion kai fylake pantos pneymatos akathartoy kai fylake pantos orneoy akathartoy kai fylake pantos thirioy akathartoy kai memisimenoy,
verses.translation: And he cried mightily with a strong voice, saying, Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird.

verses.original: ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς ⸀πέπτωκαν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς μετʼ αὐτῆς ἐπόρνευσαν, καὶ οἱ ἔμποροι τῆς γῆς ἐκ τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ στρήνους αὐτῆς ἐπλούτησαν.
verses.translit: oti ek tou oinoy tou thymou tes porneias autes peptokan panta ta ethni, kai oi vasileis tes ges met' autes eporneysan, kai oi emporoi tes ges ek tes dynameos tou strinoys autes eploytisan.
verses.translation: For all nations have drunk of the wine of the wrath of her fornication, and the kings of the earth have committed fornication with her, and the merchants of the earth are waxed rich through the abundance of her delicacies.

verses.original: Καὶ ἤκουσα ἄλλην φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ λέγουσαν· ⸀Ἐξέλθατε, ⸂ὁ λαός μου, ἐξ αὐτῆς⸃, ἵνα μὴ συγκοινωνήσητε ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις αὐτῆς, καὶ ἐκ τῶν πληγῶν αὐτῆς ἵνα μὴ λάβητε·
verses.translit: Kai ekoysa allin fonen ek tou ouranou legoysan* Exelthate, o laos moy, ex autes, ina me sygkoinonisite tais amartiais autes, kai ek ton pligon autes ina me lavite*
verses.translation: And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.

verses.original: ὅτι ἐκολλήθησαν αὐτῆς αἱ ἁμαρτίαι ἄχρι τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἐμνημόνευσεν ὁ θεὸς τὰ ἀδικήματα αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: oti ekollithisan autes ai amartiai ahri tou ouranou, kai emnimoneysen o theos ta adikimata autes.
verses.translation: For her sins have reached unto heaven, and God hath remembered her iniquities.

verses.original: ἀπόδοτε αὐτῇ ὡς καὶ αὐτὴ ἀπέδωκεν, καὶ ⸀διπλώσατε ⸀τὰ διπλᾶ κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῆς· ἐν τῷ ποτηρίῳ ᾧ ἐκέρασεν κεράσατε αὐτῇ διπλοῦν·
verses.translit: apodote aute os kai aute apedoken, kai diplosate ta dipla kata ta erga autes* en to potirio o ekerasen kerasate aute diploun*
verses.translation: Reward her even as she rewarded you, and double unto her double according to her works: in the cup which she hath filled fill to her double.

verses.original: ὅσα ἐδόξασεν αὑτὴν καὶ ἐστρηνίασεν, τοσοῦτον δότε αὐτῇ βασανισμὸν καὶ πένθος. ὅτι ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτῆς λέγει ὅτι Κάθημαι βασίλισσα, καὶ χήρα οὐκ εἰμί, καὶ πένθος οὐ μὴ ἴδω.
verses.translit: osa edoxasen auten kai estriniasen, tosouton dote aute vasanismon kai penthos. oti en te kardia autes legei oti Kathimai vasilissa, kai hira ouk eimi, kai penthos ou me ido.
verses.translation: How much she hath glorified herself, and lived deliciously, so much torment and sorrow give her: for she saith in her heart, I sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow.

verses.original: διὰ τοῦτο ἐν μιᾷ ἡμέρᾳ ἥξουσιν αἱ πληγαὶ αὐτῆς, θάνατος καὶ πένθος καὶ λιμός, καὶ ἐν πυρὶ κατακαυθήσεται· ὅτι ἰσχυρὸς κύριος ὁ θεὸς ὁ κρίνας αὐτήν.
verses.translit: dia touto en mia emera exoysin ai pligai autes, thanatos kai penthos kai limos, kai en pyri katakaythisetai* oti ishyros kyrios o theos o krinas autin.
verses.translation: Therefore shall her plagues come in one day, death, and mourning, and famine; and she shall be utterly burned with fire: for strong is the Lord God who judgeth her.

verses.original: Καὶ κλαύσουσιν καὶ κόψονται ἐπʼ αὐτὴν οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς οἱ μετʼ αὐτῆς πορνεύσαντες καὶ στρηνιάσαντες, ὅταν βλέπωσιν τὸν καπνὸν τῆς πυρώσεως αὐτῆς,
verses.translit: Kai klaysoysin kai kopsontai ep' auten oi vasileis tes ges oi met' autes porneysantes kai striniasantes, otan vleposin ton kapnon tes pyroseos autes,
verses.translation: And the kings of the earth, who have committed fornication and lived deliciously with her, shall bewail her, and lament for her, when they shall see the smoke of her burning,

verses.original: ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἑστηκότες διὰ τὸν φόβον τοῦ βασανισμοῦ αὐτῆς λέγοντες· Οὐαὶ οὐαί, ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη, Βαβυλὼν ἡ πόλις ἡ ἰσχυρά, ὅτι μιᾷ ὥρᾳ ἦλθεν ἡ κρίσις σου.
verses.translit: apo makrothen estikotes dia ton fovon tou vasanismou autes legontes* Ouai ouai, e polis e megali, Vavylon e polis e ishyra, oti mia ora elthen e krisis soy.
verses.translation: Standing afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come.

verses.original: Καὶ οἱ ἔμποροι τῆς γῆς ⸂κλαίουσιν καὶ πενθοῦσιν⸃ ἐπʼ ⸀αὐτήν, ὅτι τὸν γόμον αὐτῶν οὐδεὶς ἀγοράζει οὐκέτι,
verses.translit: Kai oi emporoi tes ges klaioysin kai penthousin ep' autin, oti ton gomon auton oudeis agorazei ouketi,
verses.translation: And the merchants of the earth shall weep and mourn over her; for no man buyeth their merchandise any more:

verses.original: γόμον χρυσοῦ καὶ ἀργύρου καὶ λίθου τιμίου καὶ ⸀μαργαριτῶν καὶ βυσσίνου καὶ ⸀πορφύρας καὶ σιρικοῦ καὶ κοκκίνου, καὶ πᾶν ξύλον θύϊνον καὶ πᾶν σκεῦος ἐλεφάντινον καὶ πᾶν σκεῦος ἐκ ξύλου τιμιωτάτου καὶ χαλκοῦ καὶ σιδήρου καὶ μαρμάρου,
verses.translit: gomon hrysou kai argyroy kai lithoy timioy kai margariton kai vyssinoy kai porfyras kai sirikou kai kokkinoy, kai pan xylon thyinon kai pan skeuos elefantinon kai pan skeuos ek xyloy timiotatoy kai halkou kai sidiroy kai marmaroy,
verses.translation: The merchandise of gold, and silver, and precious stones, and of pearls, and fine linen, and purple, and silk, and scarlet, and all thyine wood, and all manner vessels of ivory, and all manner vessels of most precious wood, and of brass, and iron, and marble,

verses.original: καὶ κιννάμωμον ⸂καὶ ἄμωμον⸃ καὶ θυμιάματα καὶ μύρον καὶ λίβανον καὶ οἶνον καὶ ἔλαιον καὶ σεμίδαλιν καὶ σῖτον καὶ ⸂κτήνη καὶ πρόβατα⸃, καὶ ἵππων καὶ ῥεδῶν καὶ σωμάτων, καὶ ψυχὰς ἀνθρώπων.
verses.translit: kai kinnamomon kai amomon kai thymiamata kai myron kai livanon kai oinon kai elaion kai semidalin kai siton kai ktini kai provata, kai ippon kai Redon kai somaton, kai psyhas anthropon.
verses.translation: And cinnamon, and odours, and ointments, and frankincense, and wine, and oil, and fine flour, and wheat, and beasts, and sheep, and horses, and chariots, and slaves, and souls of men.

verses.original: καὶ ἡ ὀπώρα ⸂σου τῆς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς ψυχῆς⸃ ἀπῆλθεν ἀπὸ σοῦ, καὶ πάντα τὰ λιπαρὰ καὶ τὰ λαμπρὰ ἀπώλετο ἀπὸ σοῦ, καὶ ⸀οὐκέτι ⸂οὐ μὴ αὐτὰ εὑρήσουσιν⸃.
verses.translit: kai e opora soy tes epithymias tes psyhes apelthen apo sou, kai panta ta lipara kai ta lampra apoleto apo sou, kai ouketi ou me auta eurisoysin.
verses.translation: And the fruits that thy soul lusted after are departed from thee, and all things which were dainty and goodly are departed from thee, and thou shalt find them no more at all.

verses.original: οἱ ἔμποροι τούτων, οἱ πλουτήσαντες ἀπʼ αὐτῆς, ἀπὸ μακρόθεν στήσονται διὰ τὸν φόβον τοῦ βασανισμοῦ αὐτῆς κλαίοντες καὶ πενθοῦντες,
verses.translit: oi emporoi toyton, oi ploytisantes ap' autes, apo makrothen stisontai dia ton fovon tou vasanismou autes klaiontes kai penthountes,
verses.translation: The merchants of these things, which were made rich by her, shall stand afar off for the fear of her torment, weeping and wailing,

verses.original: ⸀λέγοντες· Οὐαὶ οὐαί, ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη, ἡ περιβεβλημένη βύσσινον καὶ πορφυροῦν καὶ κόκκινον καὶ ⸀κεχρυσωμένη χρυσίῳ καὶ λίθῳ τιμίῳ καὶ ⸀μαργαρίτῃ,
verses.translit: legontes* Ouai ouai, e polis e megali, e perivevlimeni vyssinon kai porfyroun kai kokkinon kai kehrysomeni hrysio kai litho timio kai margarite,
verses.translation: And saying, Alas, alas, that great city, that was clothed in fine linen, and purple, and scarlet, and decked with gold, and precious stones, and pearls!

verses.original: ὅτι μιᾷ ὥρᾳ ἠρημώθη ὁ τοσοῦτος πλοῦτος. Καὶ πᾶς κυβερνήτης καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἐπὶ τόπον πλέων, καὶ ναῦται καὶ ὅσοι τὴν θάλασσαν ἐργάζονται, ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἔστησαν
verses.translit: oti mia ora erimothi o tosoutos ploutos. Kai pas kyvernitis kai pas o epi topon pleon, kai nautai kai osoi ten thalassan ergazontai, apo makrothen estisan
verses.translation: For in one hour so great riches is come to nought. And every shipmaster, and all the company in ships, and sailors, and as many as trade by sea, stood afar off,

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ἔκραξαν βλέποντες τὸν καπνὸν τῆς πυρώσεως αὐτῆς λέγοντες· Τίς ὁμοία τῇ πόλει τῇ μεγάλῃ;
verses.translit: kai ekraxan vlepontes ton kapnon tes pyroseos autes legontes* Tis omoia te polei te megale;
verses.translation: And cried when they saw the smoke of her burning, saying, What city is like unto this great city!

verses.original: καὶ ἔβαλον χοῦν ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν καὶ ⸀ἔκραξαν κλαίοντες καὶ ⸀πενθοῦντες λέγοντες· Οὐαὶ οὐαί, ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη, ἐν ᾗ ἐπλούτησαν πάντες οἱ ἔχοντες τὰ πλοῖα ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ ἐκ τῆς τιμιότητος αὐτῆς, ὅτι μιᾷ ὥρᾳ ἠρημώθη.
verses.translit: kai evalon houn epi tas kefalas auton kai ekraxan klaiontes kai penthountes legontes* Ouai ouai, e polis e megali, en e eploytisan pantes oi ehontes ta ploia en te thalasse ek tes timiotitos autes, oti mia ora erimothi.
verses.translation: And they cast dust on their heads, and cried, weeping and wailing, saying, Alas, alas, that great city, wherein were made rich all that had ships in the sea by reason of her costliness! for in one hour is she made desolate.

verses.original: Εὐφραίνου ἐπʼ αὐτῇ, οὐρανέ, καὶ οἱ ἅγιοι καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ προφῆται, ὅτι ἔκρινεν ὁ θεὸς τὸ κρίμα ὑμῶν ἐξ αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: Eufrainoy ep' aute, ourane, kai oi agioi kai oi apostoloi kai oi profetai, oti ekrinen o theos to krima umon ex autes.
verses.translation: Rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets; for God hath avenged you on her.

verses.original: Καὶ ἦρεν εἷς ἄγγελος ἰσχυρὸς λίθον ὡς ⸀μύλινον μέγαν, καὶ ἔβαλεν εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν λέγων· Οὕτως ὁρμήματι βληθήσεται Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη πόλις, καὶ οὐ μὴ εὑρεθῇ ἔτι.
verses.translit: Kai eren eis aggelos ishyros lithon os mylinon megan, kai evalen eis ten thalassan legon* Outos ormimati vlithisetai Vavylon e megali polis, kai ou me eurethe eti.
verses.translation: And a mighty angel took up a stone like a great millstone, and cast it into the sea, saying, Thus with violence shall that great city Babylon be thrown down, and shall be found no more at all.

verses.original: καὶ φωνὴ κιθαρῳδῶν καὶ μουσικῶν καὶ αὐλητῶν καὶ σαλπιστῶν οὐ μὴ ἀκουσθῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι, καὶ πᾶς τεχνίτης πάσης τέχνης οὐ μὴ εὑρεθῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι, καὶ φωνὴ μύλου οὐ μὴ ἀκουσθῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι,
verses.translit: kai fone kitharodon kai moysikon kai auliton kai salpiston ou me akoysthe en soi eti, kai pas tehnitis pasis tehnis ou me eurethe en soi eti, kai fone myloy ou me akoysthe en soi eti,
verses.translation: And the voice of harpers, and musicians, and of pipers, and trumpeters, shall be heard no more at all in thee; and no craftsman, of whatsoever craft he be , shall be found any more in thee; and the sound of a millstone shall be heard no more at all in thee;

verses.original: καὶ φῶς λύχνου οὐ μὴ φάνῃ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι, καὶ φωνὴ νυμφίου καὶ νύμφης οὐ μὴ ἀκουσθῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι· ὅτι οἱ ἔμποροί σου ἦσαν οἱ μεγιστᾶνες τῆς γῆς, ὅτι ἐν τῇ φαρμακείᾳ σου ἐπλανήθησαν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη,
verses.translit: kai fos lyhnoy ou me fane en soi eti, kai fone nymfioy kai nymfis ou me akoysthe en soi eti* oti oi emporoi soy esan oi megistanes tes ges, oti en te farmakeia soy eplanithisan panta ta ethni,
verses.translation: And the light of a candle shall shine no more at all in thee; and the voice of the bridegroom and of the bride shall be heard no more at all in thee: for thy merchants were the great men of the earth; for by thy sorceries were all nations deceived.

verses.original: καὶ ἐν αὐτῇ ⸀αἷμα προφητῶν καὶ ἁγίων εὑρέθη καὶ πάντων τῶν ἐσφαγμένων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
verses.translit: kai en aute aima profiton kai agion eurethi kai panton ton esfagmenon epi tes ges.
verses.translation: And in her was found the blood of prophets, and of saints, and of all that were slain upon the earth.

verses.original: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἤκουσα ὡς φωνὴν μεγάλην ὄχλου πολλοῦ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ λεγόντων· Ἁλληλουϊά· ἡ σωτηρία καὶ ἡ ⸂δόξα καὶ ἡ δύναμις⸃ τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν,
verses.translit: Meta tauta ekoysa os fonen megalin ohloy pollou en to ourano legonton* Alliloyia* e sotiria kai e doxa kai e dynamis tou theou emon,
verses.translation: And after these things I heard a great voice of much people in heaven, saying, Alleluia; Salvation, and glory, and honour, and power, unto the Lord our God:

verses.original: ὅτι ἀληθιναὶ καὶ δίκαιαι αἱ κρίσεις αὐτοῦ· ὅτι ἔκρινεν τὴν πόρνην τὴν μεγάλην ἥτις ⸀ἔφθειρεν τὴν γῆν ἐν τῇ πορνείᾳ αὐτῆς, καὶ ἐξεδίκησεν τὸ αἷμα τῶν δούλων αὐτοῦ ἐκ χειρὸς αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: oti alithinai kai dikaiai ai kriseis autou* oti ekrinen ten pornin ten megalin etis eftheiren ten gen en te porneia autes, kai exedikisen to aima ton doylon autou ek heiros autes.
verses.translation: For true and righteous are his judgments: for he hath judged the great whore, which did corrupt the earth with her fornication, and hath avenged the blood of his servants at her hand.

verses.original: καὶ δεύτερον ⸀εἴρηκαν· Ἁλληλουϊά· καὶ ὁ καπνὸς αὐτῆς ἀναβαίνει εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων.
verses.translit: kai deyteron eirikan* Alliloyia* kai o kapnos autes anavainei eis tous aionas ton aionon.
verses.translation: And again they said, Alleluia. And her smoke rose up for ever and ever.

verses.original: καὶ ἔπεσαν οἱ πρεσβύτεροι οἱ εἴκοσι τέσσαρες καὶ τὰ τέσσαρα ζῷα, καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ θεῷ τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ ⸂τῷ θρόνῳ⸃ λέγοντες· Ἀμήν, Ἁλληλουϊά.
verses.translit: kai epesan oi presvyteroi oi eikosi tessares kai ta tessara zoa, kai prosekynisan to theo to kathimeno epi to throno legontes* Amin, Alliloyia.
verses.translation: And the four and twenty elders and the four beasts fell down and worshipped God that sat on the throne, saying, Amen; Alleluia.

verses.original: Καὶ φωνὴ ἀπὸ τοῦ θρόνου ἐξῆλθεν λέγουσα· Αἰνεῖτε ⸂τῷ θεῷ⸃ ἡμῶν, πάντες οἱ δοῦλοι αὐτοῦ, ⸀καὶ οἱ φοβούμενοι αὐτόν, οἱ μικροὶ καὶ οἱ μεγάλοι.
verses.translit: Kai fone apo tou thronoy exelthen legoysa* Aineite to theo emon, pantes oi douloi autou, kai oi fovoymenoi auton, oi mikroi kai oi megaloi.
verses.translation: And a voice came out of the throne, saying, Praise our God, all ye his servants, and ye that fear him, both small and great.

verses.original: καὶ ἤκουσα ὡς φωνὴν ὄχλου πολλοῦ καὶ ὡς φωνὴν ὑδάτων πολλῶν καὶ ὡς φωνὴν βροντῶν ἰσχυρῶν, ⸀λεγόντων· Ἁλληλουϊά, ὅτι ἐβασίλευσεν κύριος, ὁ ⸀θεός, ὁ παντοκράτωρ.
verses.translit: kai ekoysa os fonen ohloy pollou kai os fonen udaton pollon kai os fonen vronton ishyron, legonton* Alliloyia, oti evasileysen kyrios, o theos, o pantokrator.
verses.translation: And I heard as it were the voice of a great multitude, and as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of mighty thunderings, saying, Alleluia: for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth.

verses.original: χαίρωμεν καὶ ⸀ἀγαλλιῶμεν, καὶ ⸀δώσομεν τὴν δόξαν αὐτῷ, ὅτι ἦλθεν ὁ γάμος τοῦ ἀρνίου, καὶ ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ ἡτοίμασεν ἑαυτήν,
verses.translit: hairomen kai agalliomen, kai dosomen ten doxan auto, oti elthen o gamos tou arnioy, kai e gyne autou etoimasen eaytin,
verses.translation: Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready.

verses.original: καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῇ ἵνα περιβάληται βύσσινον ⸀λαμπρὸν καθαρόν, τὸ γὰρ βύσσινον τὰ δικαιώματα τῶν ἁγίων ἐστίν.
verses.translit: kai edothi aute ina perivalitai vyssinon lampron katharon, to gar vyssinon ta dikaiomata ton agion estin.
verses.translation: And to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints.

verses.original: Καὶ λέγει μοι· Γράψον· Μακάριοι οἱ εἰς τὸ δεῖπνον τοῦ γάμου τοῦ ἀρνίου κεκλημένοι. καὶ λέγει μοι· Οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι ἀληθινοὶ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσιν.
verses.translit: Kai legei moi* Grapson* Makarioi oi eis to deipnon tou gamoy tou arnioy keklimenoi. kai legei moi* Outoi oi logoi alithinoi tou theou eisin.
verses.translation: And he saith unto me, Write, Blessed are they which are called unto the marriage supper of the Lamb. And he saith unto me, These are the true sayings of God.

verses.original: καὶ ἔπεσα ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ προσκυνῆσαι αὐτῷ. καὶ λέγει μοι· Ὅρα μή· σύνδουλός σού εἰμι καὶ τῶν ἀδελφῶν σου τῶν ἐχόντων τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ· τῷ θεῷ προσκύνησον· ἡ γὰρ ⸀μαρτυρία Ἰησοῦ ἐστιν τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς προφητείας.
verses.translit: kai epesa emprosthen ton podon autou proskynesai auto. kai legei moi* Ora mi* syndoylos soy eimi kai ton adelfon soy ton ehonton ten martyrian Iisou* to theo proskynison* e gar martyria Iisou estin to pneuma tes profiteias.
verses.translation: And I fell at his feet to worship him. And he said unto me, See thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren that have the testimony of Jesus: worship God: for the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶδον τὸν οὐρανὸν ἠνεῳγμένον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἵππος λευκός, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπʼ αὐτὸν ⸂πιστὸς καλούμενος⸃ καὶ ἀληθινός, καὶ ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ κρίνει καὶ πολεμεῖ.
verses.translit: Kai eidon ton ouranon eneogmenon, kai idou ippos leykos, kai o kathimenos ep' auton pistos kaloymenos kai alithinos, kai en dikaiosyne krinei kai polemei.
verses.translation: And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ὀφθαλμοὶ ⸀αὐτοῦ φλὸξ πυρός, καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ διαδήματα πολλά, ⸀ἔχων ὄνομα γεγραμμένον ὃ οὐδεὶς οἶδεν εἰ μὴ αὐτός,
verses.translit: oi de ofthalmoi autou flox pyros, kai epi ten kefalen autou diadimata polla, ehon onoma gegrammenon o oudeis oiden ei me autos,
verses.translation: His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself.

verses.original: καὶ περιβεβλημένος ἱμάτιον ⸀βεβαμμένον αἵματι, καὶ ⸀κέκληται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ὁ Λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ.
verses.translit: kai perivevlimenos imation vevammenon aimati, kai keklitai to onoma autou o Logos tou Theou.
verses.translation: And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God.

verses.original: καὶ τὰ στρατεύματα ⸀τὰ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ ἐφʼ ἵπποις λευκοῖς, ἐνδεδυμένοι βύσσινον λευκὸν καθαρόν.
verses.translit: kai ta strateymata ta en to ourano ekoloythei auto ef' ippois leykois, endedymenoi vyssinon leykon katharon.
verses.translation: And the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean.

verses.original: καὶ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ ἐκπορεύεται ⸀ῥομφαία ὀξεῖα, ἵνα ἐν αὐτῇ πατάξῃ τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ αὐτὸς ποιμανεῖ αὐτοὺς ἐν ῥάβδῳ σιδηρᾷ· καὶ αὐτὸς πατεῖ τὴν ληνὸν τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τῆς ὀργῆς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ παντοκράτορος.
verses.translit: kai ek tou stomatos autou ekporeyetai Romfaia oxeia, ina en aute pataxe ta ethni, kai autos poimanei autous en Ravdo sidira* kai autos patei ten linon tou oinoy tou thymou tes orges tou theou tou pantokratoros.
verses.translation: And out of his mouth goeth a sharp sword, that with it he should smite the nations: and he shall rule them with a rod of iron: and he treadeth the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of Almighty God.

verses.original: καὶ ἔχει ἐπὶ τὸ ἱμάτιον καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν μηρὸν αὐτοῦ ὄνομα γεγραμμένον· Βασιλεὺς βασιλέων καὶ κύριος κυρίων.
verses.translit: kai ehei epi to imation kai epi ton miron autou onoma gegrammenon* Vasileus vasileon kai kyrios kyrion.
verses.translation: And he hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶδον ⸀ἕνα ἄγγελον ἑστῶτα ἐν τῷ ἡλίῳ, καὶ ⸀ἔκραξεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγων πᾶσι τοῖς ὀρνέοις τοῖς πετομένοις ἐν μεσουρανήματι· Δεῦτε συνάχθητε εἰς τὸ δεῖπνον τὸ μέγα τοῦ θεοῦ,
verses.translit: Kai eidon ena aggelon estota en to elio, kai ekraxen fone megale legon pasi tois orneois tois petomenois en mesoyranimati* Deute synahthite eis to deipnon to mega tou theou,
verses.translation: And I saw an angel standing in the sun; and he cried with a loud voice, saying to all the fowls that fly in the midst of heaven, Come and gather yourselves together unto the supper of the great God;

verses.original: ἵνα φάγητε σάρκας βασιλέων καὶ σάρκας χιλιάρχων καὶ σάρκας ἰσχυρῶν καὶ σάρκας ἵππων καὶ τῶν καθημένων ἐπʼ ⸀αὐτῶν, καὶ σάρκας πάντων ἐλευθέρων τε καὶ δούλων καὶ μικρῶν ⸀καὶ μεγάλων.
verses.translit: ina fagite sarkas vasileon kai sarkas hiliarhon kai sarkas ishyron kai sarkas ippon kai ton kathimenon ep' auton, kai sarkas panton eleytheron te kai doylon kai mikron kai megalon.
verses.translation: That ye may eat the flesh of kings, and the flesh of captains, and the flesh of mighty men, and the flesh of horses, and of them that sit on them, and the flesh of all men, both free and bond, both small and great.

verses.original: καὶ εἶδον τὸ θηρίον καὶ τοὺς βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς καὶ τὰ στρατεύματα αὐτῶν συνηγμένα ποιῆσαι ⸀τὸν πόλεμον μετὰ τοῦ καθημένου ἐπὶ τοῦ ἵππου καὶ μετὰ τοῦ στρατεύματος αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai eidon to thirion kai tous vasileis tes ges kai ta strateymata auton synigmena poiesai ton polemon meta tou kathimenoy epi tou ippoy kai meta tou strateymatos autou.
verses.translation: And I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse, and against his army.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπιάσθη τὸ θηρίον καὶ ⸂μετʼ αὐτοῦ ὁ⸃ ψευδοπροφήτης ὁ ποιήσας τὰ σημεῖα ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ, ἐν οἷς ἐπλάνησεν τοὺς λαβόντας τὸ χάραγμα τοῦ θηρίου καὶ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας τῇ εἰκόνι αὐτοῦ· ζῶντες ἐβλήθησαν οἱ δύο εἰς τὴν λίμνην τοῦ πυρὸς ⸂τῆς καιομένης⸃ ἐν θείῳ.
verses.translit: kai epiasthi to thirion kai met' autou o pseydoprofitis o poiisas ta simeia enopion autou, en ois eplanisen tous lavontas to haragma tou thirioy kai tous proskynountas te eikoni autou* zontes evlithisan oi dyo eis ten limnin tou pyros tes kaiomenis en theio.
verses.translation: And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet that wrought miracles before him, with which he deceived them that had received the mark of the beast, and them that worshipped his image. These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone.

verses.original: καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ ἀπεκτάνθησαν ἐν τῇ ῥομφαίᾳ τοῦ καθημένου ἐπὶ τοῦ ἵππου τῇ ἐξελθούσῃ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ, καὶ πάντα τὰ ὄρνεα ἐχορτάσθησαν ἐκ τῶν σαρκῶν αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai oi loipoi apektanthisan en te Romfaia tou kathimenoy epi tou ippoy te exelthoyse ek tou stomatos autou, kai panta ta ornea ehortasthisan ek ton sarkon auton.
verses.translation: And the remnant were slain with the sword of him that sat upon the horse, which sword proceeded out of his mouth: and all the fowls were filled with their flesh.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶδον ἄγγελον καταβαίνοντα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ἔχοντα τὴν κλεῖν τῆς ἀβύσσου καὶ ἅλυσιν μεγάλην ἐπὶ τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Kai eidon aggelon katavainonta ek tou ouranou, ehonta ten klein tes avyssoy kai alysin megalin epi ten heira autou.
verses.translation: And I saw an angel come down from heaven, having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand.

verses.original: καὶ ἐκράτησεν τὸν δράκοντα, ⸂ὁ ὄφις ὁ ἀρχαῖος⸃, ὅς ἐστιν Διάβολος καὶ ὁ ⸀Σατανᾶς, καὶ ἔδησεν αὐτὸν χίλια ἔτη,
verses.translit: kai ekratisen ton drakonta, o ofis o arhaios, os estin Diavolos kai o Satanas, kai edisen auton hilia eti,
verses.translation: And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years,

verses.original: καὶ ἔβαλεν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν ἄβυσσον, καὶ ἔκλεισεν καὶ ἐσφράγισεν ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ, ἵνα μὴ ⸀πλανήσῃ ἔτι τὰ ἔθνη, ἄχρι τελεσθῇ τὰ χίλια ἔτη· ⸀μετὰ ταῦτα δεῖ ⸂λυθῆναι αὐτὸν⸃ μικρὸν χρόνον.
verses.translit: kai evalen auton eis ten avysson, kai ekleisen kai esfragisen epano autou, ina me planise eti ta ethni, ahri telesthe ta hilia eti* meta tauta dei lythenai auton mikron hronon.
verses.translation: And cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should deceive the nations no more, till the thousand years should be fulfilled: and after that he must be loosed a little season.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶδον θρόνους, καὶ ἐκάθισαν ἐπʼ αὐτούς, καὶ κρίμα ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς, καὶ τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν πεπελεκισμένων διὰ τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ καὶ διὰ τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ οἵτινες οὐ προσεκύνησαν τὸ θηρίον οὐδὲ τὴν εἰκόνα αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἔλαβον τὸ χάραγμα ἐπὶ τὸ μέτωπον καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν χεῖρα αὐτῶν· καὶ ἔζησαν καὶ ἐβασίλευσαν μετὰ τοῦ χριστοῦ ⸀χίλια ἔτη.
verses.translit: Kai eidon thronoys, kai ekathisan ep' autoys, kai krima edothi autois, kai tas psyhas ton pepelekismenon dia ten martyrian Iisou kai dia ton logon tou theou, kai oitines ou prosekynisan to thirion oude ten eikona autou kai ouk elavon to haragma epi to metopon kai epi ten heira auton* kai ezisan kai evasileysan meta tou hristou hilia eti.
verses.translation: And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.

verses.original: ⸀οἱ λοιποὶ τῶν νεκρῶν οὐκ ἔζησαν ἄχρι τελεσθῇ τὰ χίλια ἔτη. αὕτη ἡ ἀνάστασις ἡ πρώτη.
verses.translit: oi loipoi ton nekron ouk ezisan ahri telesthe ta hilia eti. auti e anastasis e proti.
verses.translation: But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished. This is the first resurrection.

verses.original: μακάριος καὶ ἅγιος ὁ ἔχων μέρος ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει τῇ πρώτῃ· ἐπὶ τούτων ὁ δεύτερος θάνατος οὐκ ἔχει ἐξουσίαν, ἀλλʼ ἔσονται ἱερεῖς τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ χριστοῦ, καὶ βασιλεύσουσιν μετʼ αὐτοῦ ⸀χίλια ἔτη.
verses.translit: makarios kai agios o ehon meros en te anastasei te prote* epi toyton o deyteros thanatos ouk ehei exoysian, all' esontai iereis tou theou kai tou hristou, kai vasileysoysin met' autou hilia eti.
verses.translation: Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection: on such the second death hath no power, but they shall be priests of God and of Christ, and shall reign with him a thousand years.

verses.original: Καὶ ὅταν τελεσθῇ τὰ χίλια ἔτη, λυθήσεται ὁ Σατανᾶς ἐκ τῆς φυλακῆς αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: Kai otan telesthe ta hilia eti, lythisetai o Satanas ek tes fylakes autou,
verses.translation: And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison,

verses.original: καὶ ἐξελεύσεται πλανῆσαι τὰ ἔθνη τὰ ἐν ταῖς τέσσαρσι γωνίαις τῆς γῆς, τὸν Γὼγ ⸀καὶ Μαγώγ, συναγαγεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν πόλεμον, ὧν ὁ ἀριθμὸς ⸀αὐτῶν ὡς ἡ ἄμμος τῆς θαλάσσης.
verses.translit: kai exeleysetai planesai ta ethni ta en tais tessarsi goniais tes ges, ton Gog kai Magog, synagagein autous eis ton polemon, on o arithmos auton os e ammos tes thalassis.
verses.translation: And shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them together to battle: the number of whom is as the sand of the sea.

verses.original: καὶ ἀνέβησαν ἐπὶ τὸ πλάτος τῆς γῆς, καὶ ⸀ἐκύκλευσαν τὴν παρεμβολὴν τῶν ἁγίων καὶ τὴν πόλιν τὴν ἠγαπημένην. καὶ κατέβη πῦρ ⸂ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ⸃ καὶ κατέφαγεν αὐτούς·
verses.translit: kai anevisan epi to platos tes ges, kai ekykleysan ten paremvolen ton agion kai ten polin ten egapimenin. kai katevi pur ek tou ouranou kai katefagen autoys*
verses.translation: And they went up on the breadth of the earth, and compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city: and fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them.

verses.original: καὶ ὁ διάβολος ὁ πλανῶν αὐτοὺς ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν λίμνην τοῦ πυρὸς καὶ θείου, ὅπου καὶ τὸ θηρίον καὶ ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης, καὶ βασανισθήσονται ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων.
verses.translit: kai o diavolos o planon autous evlithi eis ten limnin tou pyros kai theioy, opoy kai to thirion kai o pseydoprofitis, kai vasanisthisontai emeras kai nyktos eis tous aionas ton aionon.
verses.translation: And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are , and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶδον θρόνον μέγαν λευκὸν καὶ τὸν καθήμενον ⸂ἐπʼ αὐτοῦ⸃, οὗ ἀπὸ ⸀τοῦ προσώπου ἔφυγεν ἡ γῆ καὶ ὁ οὐρανός, καὶ τόπος οὐχ εὑρέθη αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: Kai eidon thronon megan leykon kai ton kathimenon ep' autou, ou apo tou prosopoy efygen e ge kai o ouranos, kai topos ouh eurethi autois.
verses.translation: And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them.

verses.original: καὶ εἶδον τοὺς νεκρούς, τοὺς μεγάλους καὶ τοὺς μικρούς, ἑστῶτας ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου, καὶ βιβλία ἠνοίχθησαν· καὶ ἄλλο βιβλίον ἠνοίχθη, ὅ ἐστιν τῆς ζωῆς· καὶ ἐκρίθησαν οἱ νεκροὶ ἐκ τῶν γεγραμμένων ἐν τοῖς βιβλίοις κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai eidon tous nekroys, tous megaloys kai tous mikroys, estotas enopion tou thronoy, kai vivlia enoihthisan* kai allo vivlion enoihthi, o estin tes zoes* kai ekrithisan oi nekroi ek ton gegrammenon en tois vivliois kata ta erga auton.
verses.translation: And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.

verses.original: καὶ ἔδωκεν ἡ θάλασσα τοὺς νεκροὺς τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ, καὶ ὁ θάνατος καὶ ὁ ᾅδης ἔδωκαν τοὺς νεκροὺς τοὺς ἐν αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἐκρίθησαν ἕκαστος κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai edoken e thalassa tous nekrous tous en aute, kai o thanatos kai o adis edokan tous nekrous tous en autois, kai ekrithisan ekastos kata ta erga auton.
verses.translation: And the sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them: and they were judged every man according to their works.

verses.original: καὶ ὁ θάνατος καὶ ὁ ᾅδης ἐβλήθησαν εἰς τὴν λίμνην τοῦ πυρός. οὗτος ὁ ⸂θάνατος ὁ δεύτερός⸃ ἐστιν, ἡ λίμνη τοῦ πυρός.
verses.translit: kai o thanatos kai o adis evlithisan eis ten limnin tou pyros. outos o thanatos o deyteros estin, e limni tou pyros.
verses.translation: And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.

verses.original: καὶ εἴ τις οὐχ εὑρέθη ἐν ⸂τῇ βίβλῳ⸃ τῆς ζωῆς γεγραμμένος, ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν λίμνην τοῦ πυρός.
verses.translit: kai ei tis ouh eurethi en te vivlo tes zoes gegrammenos, evlithi eis ten limnin tou pyros.
verses.translation: And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶδον οὐρανὸν καινὸν καὶ γῆν καινήν· ὁ γὰρ πρῶτος οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ πρώτη γῆ ἀπῆλθαν, καὶ ἡ θάλασσα οὐκ ἔστιν ἔτι.
verses.translit: Kai eidon ouranon kainon kai gen kainin* o gar protos ouranos kai e proti ge apelthan, kai e thalassa ouk estin eti.
verses.translation: And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea.

verses.original: καὶ τὴν πόλιν τὴν ἁγίαν Ἰερουσαλὴμ καινὴν εἶδον καταβαίνουσαν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἡτοιμασμένην ὡς νύμφην κεκοσμημένην τῷ ἀνδρὶ αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: kai ten polin ten agian Ieroysalem kainen eidon katavainoysan ek tou ouranou apo tou theou, etoimasmenin os nymfin kekosmimenin to andri autes.
verses.translation: And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.

verses.original: καὶ ἤκουσα φωνῆς μεγάλης ἐκ τοῦ ⸀θρόνου λεγούσης· Ἰδοὺ ἡ σκηνὴ τοῦ θεοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ σκηνώσει μετʼ αὐτῶν, καὶ αὐτοὶ ⸀λαοὶ αὐτοῦ ἔσονται, καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ θεὸς ⸂μετʼ αὐτῶν ἔσται⸃,
verses.translit: kai ekoysa fones megalis ek tou thronoy legoysis* Idou e skine tou theou meta ton anthropon, kai skinosei met' auton, kai autoi laoi autou esontai, kai autos o theos met' auton estai,
verses.translation: And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξαλείψει πᾶν δάκρυον ⸀ἐκ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν, καὶ ὁ θάνατος οὐκ ἔσται ἔτι· οὔτε πένθος οὔτε κραυγὴ οὔτε πόνος οὐκ ἔσται ⸀ἔτι. τὰ πρῶτα ἀπῆλθαν.
verses.translit: kai exaleipsei pan dakryon ek ton ofthalmon auton, kai o thanatos ouk estai eti* oute penthos oute krayge oute ponos ouk estai eti. ta prota apelthan.
verses.translation: And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῷ θρόνῳ· Ἰδοὺ ⸂καινὰ ποιῶ πάντα⸃. καὶ ⸀λέγει· Γράψον, ὅτι οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι ⸂πιστοὶ καὶ ἀληθινοί⸃ εἰσιν.
verses.translit: Kai eipen o kathimenos epi to throno* Idou kaina poio panta. kai legei* Grapson, oti outoi oi logoi pistoi kai alithinoi eisin.
verses.translation: And he that sat upon the throne said, Behold, I make all things new. And he said unto me, Write: for these words are true and faithful.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπέν μοι· ⸂Γέγοναν. ἐγὼ⸃ τὸ Ἄλφα καὶ τὸ Ὦ, ἡ ἀρχὴ καὶ τὸ τέλος. ἐγὼ τῷ διψῶντι δώσω ἐκ τῆς πηγῆς τοῦ ὕδατος τῆς ζωῆς δωρεάν.
verses.translit: kai eipen moi* Gegonan. ego to Alfa kai to O, e arhe kai to telos. ego to dipsonti doso ek tes piges tou udatos tes zoes dorean.
verses.translation: And he said unto me, It is done. I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely.

verses.original: ὁ νικῶν κληρονομήσει ταῦτα, καὶ ἔσομαι αὐτῷ θεὸς καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσται μοι υἱός.
verses.translit: o nikon klironomisei tauta, kai esomai auto theos kai autos estai moi yios.
verses.translation: He that overcometh shall inherit all things; and I will be his God, and he shall be my son.

verses.original: τοῖς δὲ δειλοῖς καὶ ⸀ἀπίστοις καὶ ἐβδελυγμένοις καὶ φονεῦσι καὶ πόρνοις καὶ φαρμάκοις καὶ εἰδωλολάτραις καὶ πᾶσι τοῖς ψευδέσιν τὸ μέρος αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ λίμνῃ τῇ καιομένῃ πυρὶ καὶ θείῳ, ὅ ἐστιν ὁ θάνατος ὁ δεύτερος.
verses.translit: tois de deilois kai apistois kai evdelygmenois kai foneusi kai pornois kai farmakois kai eidololatrais kai pasi tois pseydesin to meros auton en te limne te kaiomene pyri kai theio, o estin o thanatos o deyteros.
verses.translation: But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death.

verses.original: Καὶ ἦλθεν εἷς ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλων τῶν ἐχόντων τὰς ἑπτὰ φιάλας, ⸂τῶν γεμόντων⸃ τῶν ἑπτὰ πληγῶν τῶν ἐσχάτων, καὶ ἐλάλησεν μετʼ ἐμοῦ λέγων· Δεῦρο, δείξω σοι τὴν ⸂νύμφην τὴν γυναῖκα⸃ τοῦ ἀρνίου.
verses.translit: Kai elthen eis ek ton epta aggelon ton ehonton tas epta fialas, ton gemonton ton epta pligon ton eshaton, kai elalisen met' emou legon* Deuro, deixo soi ten nymfin ten gynaika tou arnioy.
verses.translation: And there came unto me one of the seven angels which had the seven vials full of the seven last plagues, and talked with me, saying, Come hither, I will shew thee the bride, the Lamb’s wife.

verses.original: καὶ ἀπήνεγκέν με ἐν πνεύματι ἐπὶ ὄρος μέγα καὶ ὑψηλόν, καὶ ἔδειξέν μοι τὴν ⸀πόλιν τὴν ἁγίαν Ἰερουσαλὴμ καταβαίνουσαν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ,
verses.translit: kai apinegken me en pneymati epi oros mega kai upsilon, kai edeixen moi ten polin ten agian Ieroysalem katavainoysan ek tou ouranou apo tou theou,
verses.translation: And he carried me away in the spirit to a great and high mountain, and shewed me that great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God,

verses.original: ἔχουσαν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ θεοῦ· ὁ φωστὴρ αὐτῆς ὅμοιος λίθῳ τιμιωτάτῳ, ὡς λίθῳ ἰάσπιδι κρυσταλλίζοντι·
verses.translit: ehoysan ten doxan tou theou* o foster autes omoios litho timiotato, os litho iaspidi krystallizonti*
verses.translation: Having the glory of God: and her light was like unto a stone most precious, even like a jasper stone, clear as crystal;

verses.original: ἔχουσα τεῖχος μέγα καὶ ὑψηλόν, ἔχουσα πυλῶνας δώδεκα, καὶ ἐπὶ ⸂τοῖς πυλῶσιν⸃ ἀγγέλους δώδεκα, καὶ ὀνόματα ἐπιγεγραμμένα ἅ ⸀ἐστιν τῶν δώδεκα ⸀φυλῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ·
verses.translit: ehoysa teihos mega kai upsilon, ehoysa pylonas dodeka, kai epi tois pylosin aggeloys dodeka, kai onomata epigegrammena a estin ton dodeka fylon yion Israil*
verses.translation: And had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel:

verses.original: ἀπὸ ⸀ἀνατολῆς πυλῶνες τρεῖς, καὶ ἀπὸ βορρᾶ πυλῶνες τρεῖς, καὶ ἀπὸ νότου πυλῶνες τρεῖς, καὶ ἀπὸ δυσμῶν πυλῶνες τρεῖς·
verses.translit: apo anatoles pylones treis, kai apo vorra pylones treis, kai apo notoy pylones treis, kai apo dysmon pylones treis*
verses.translation: On the east three gates; on the north three gates; on the south three gates; and on the west three gates.

verses.original: καὶ τὸ τεῖχος τῆς πόλεως ⸀ἔχων θεμελίους δώδεκα, καὶ ἐπʼ αὐτῶν δώδεκα ὀνόματα τῶν δώδεκα ἀποστόλων τοῦ ἀρνίου.
verses.translit: kai to teihos tes poleos ehon themelioys dodeka, kai ep' auton dodeka onomata ton dodeka apostolon tou arnioy.
verses.translation: And the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ λαλῶν μετʼ ἐμοῦ εἶχεν μέτρον κάλαμον χρυσοῦν, ἵνα μετρήσῃ τὴν πόλιν καὶ τοὺς πυλῶνας αὐτῆς καὶ τὸ τεῖχος αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: Kai o lalon met' emou eihen metron kalamon hrysoun, ina metrise ten polin kai tous pylonas autes kai to teihos autes.
verses.translation: And he that talked with me had a golden reed to measure the city, and the gates thereof, and the wall thereof.

verses.original: καὶ ἡ πόλις τετράγωνος κεῖται, καὶ τὸ μῆκος αὐτῆς ⸀ὅσον τὸ πλάτος. καὶ ἐμέτρησεν τὴν πόλιν τῷ καλάμῳ ἐπὶ ⸀σταδίους δώδεκα ⸀χιλιάδων· τὸ μῆκος καὶ τὸ πλάτος καὶ τὸ ὕψος αὐτῆς ἴσα ἐστίν.
verses.translit: kai e polis tetragonos keitai, kai to mekos autes oson to platos. kai emetrisen ten polin to kalamo epi stadioys dodeka hiliadon* to mekos kai to platos kai to upsos autes isa estin.
verses.translation: And the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal.

verses.original: καὶ ἐμέτρησεν τὸ τεῖχος αὐτῆς ἑκατὸν τεσσεράκοντα τεσσάρων πηχῶν, μέτρον ἀνθρώπου, ὅ ἐστιν ἀγγέλου.
verses.translit: kai emetrisen to teihos autes ekaton tesserakonta tessaron pihon, metron anthropoy, o estin aggeloy.
verses.translation: And he measured the wall thereof, an hundred and forty and four cubits, according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel.

verses.original: ⸀καὶ ἡ ἐνδώμησις τοῦ τείχους αὐτῆς ἴασπις, καὶ ἡ πόλις χρυσίον καθαρὸν ὅμοιον ὑάλῳ καθαρῷ·
verses.translit: kai e endomisis tou teihoys autes iaspis, kai e polis hrysion katharon omoion ualo katharo*
verses.translation: And the building of the wall of it was of jasper: and the city was pure gold, like unto clear glass.

verses.original: ⸀οἱ θεμέλιοι τοῦ τείχους τῆς πόλεως παντὶ λίθῳ τιμίῳ κεκοσμημένοι· ὁ θεμέλιος ὁ πρῶτος ἴασπις, ὁ δεύτερος σάπφιρος, ὁ τρίτος χαλκηδών, ὁ τέταρτος σμάραγδος,
verses.translit: oi themelioi tou teihoys tes poleos panti litho timio kekosmimenoi* o themelios o protos iaspis, o deyteros sapfiros, o tritos halkidon, o tetartos smaragdos,
verses.translation: And the foundations of the wall of the city were garnished with all manner of precious stones. The first foundation was jasper; the second, sapphire; the third, a chalcedony; the fourth, an emerald;

verses.original: ὁ πέμπτος σαρδόνυξ, ὁ ἕκτος σάρδιον, ὁ ἕβδομος χρυσόλιθος, ὁ ὄγδοος βήρυλλος, ὁ ἔνατος τοπάζιον, ὁ δέκατος χρυσόπρασος, ὁ ἑνδέκατος ὑάκινθος, ὁ δωδέκατος ἀμέθυστος·
verses.translit: o pemptos sardonyx, o ektos sardion, o evdomos hrysolithos, o ogdoos viryllos, o enatos topazion, o dekatos hrysoprasos, o endekatos uakinthos, o dodekatos amethystos*
verses.translation: The fifth, sardonyx; the sixth, sardius; the seventh, chrysolite; the eighth, beryl; the ninth, a topaz; the tenth, a chrysoprasus; the eleventh, a jacinth; the twelfth, an amethyst.

verses.original: καὶ οἱ δώδεκα πυλῶνες δώδεκα μαργαρῖται, ἀνὰ εἷς ἕκαστος τῶν πυλώνων ἦν ἐξ ἑνὸς μαργαρίτου· καὶ ἡ πλατεῖα τῆς πόλεως χρυσίον καθαρὸν ὡς ὕαλος διαυγής.
verses.translit: kai oi dodeka pylones dodeka margaritai, ana eis ekastos ton pylonon en ex enos margaritoy* kai e plateia tes poleos hrysion katharon os ualos diaygis.
verses.translation: And the twelve gates were twelve pearls; every several gate was of one pearl: and the street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass.

verses.original: Καὶ ναὸν οὐκ εἶδον ἐν αὐτῇ, ὁ γὰρ κύριος, ὁ θεός, ὁ παντοκράτωρ, ναὸς αὐτῆς ἐστιν, καὶ τὸ ἀρνίον.
verses.translit: Kai naon ouk eidon en aute, o gar kyrios, o theos, o pantokrator, naos autes estin, kai to arnion.
verses.translation: And I saw no temple therein: for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it.

verses.original: καὶ ἡ πόλις οὐ χρείαν ἔχει τοῦ ἡλίου οὐδὲ τῆς σελήνης, ἵνα φαίνωσιν αὐτῇ, ἡ γὰρ δόξα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐφώτισεν αὐτήν, καὶ ὁ λύχνος αὐτῆς τὸ ἀρνίον.
verses.translit: kai e polis ou hreian ehei tou elioy oude tes selinis, ina fainosin aute, e gar doxa tou theou efotisen autin, kai o lyhnos autes to arnion.
verses.translation: And the city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it: for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof.

verses.original: καὶ περιπατήσουσιν τὰ ἔθνη διὰ τοῦ φωτὸς αὐτῆς· καὶ οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς φέρουσιν ⸂τὴν δόξαν αὐτῶν⸃ εἰς αὐτήν·
verses.translit: kai peripatisoysin ta ethni dia tou fotos autes* kai oi vasileis tes ges feroysin ten doxan auton eis autin*
verses.translation: And the nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it: and the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it.

verses.original: καὶ οἱ πυλῶνες αὐτῆς οὐ μὴ κλεισθῶσιν ἡμέρας, νὺξ γὰρ οὐκ ἔσται ἐκεῖ,
verses.translit: kai oi pylones autes ou me kleisthosin emeras, nux gar ouk estai ekei,
verses.translation: And the gates of it shall not be shut at all by day: for there shall be no night there.

verses.original: καὶ οἴσουσιν τὴν δόξαν καὶ τὴν τιμὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν εἰς αὐτήν.
verses.translit: kai oisoysin ten doxan kai ten timen ton ethnon eis autin.
verses.translation: And they shall bring the glory and honour of the nations into it.

verses.original: καὶ οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς αὐτὴν πᾶν κοινὸν καὶ ⸀ποιῶν βδέλυγμα καὶ ψεῦδος, εἰ μὴ οἱ γεγραμμένοι ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τῆς ζωῆς τοῦ ἀρνίου.
verses.translit: kai ou me eiselthe eis auten pan koinon kai poion vdelygma kai pseudos, ei me oi gegrammenoi en to vivlio tes zoes tou arnioy.
verses.translation: And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔδειξέν μοι ⸀ποταμὸν ὕδατος ζωῆς λαμπρὸν ὡς κρύσταλλον, ἐκπορευόμενον ἐκ τοῦ θρόνου τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἀρνίου
verses.translit: Kai edeixen moi potamon udatos zoes lampron os krystallon, ekporeyomenon ek tou thronoy tou theou kai tou arnioy
verses.translation: And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb.

verses.original: ἐν μέσῳ τῆς πλατείας αὐτῆς· καὶ τοῦ ποταμοῦ ἐντεῦθεν καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ξύλον ζωῆς ποιοῦν καρποὺς δώδεκα, κατὰ μῆνα ἕκαστον ⸀ἀποδιδοῦν τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὰ φύλλα τοῦ ξύλου εἰς θεραπείαν τῶν ἐθνῶν.
verses.translit: en meso tes plateias autes* kai tou potamou enteuthen kai ekeithen xylon zoes poioun karpous dodeka, kata mena ekaston apodidoun ton karpon autou, kai ta fylla tou xyloy eis therapeian ton ethnon.
verses.translation: In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.

verses.original: καὶ πᾶν κατάθεμα οὐκ ἔσται ἔτι. καὶ ὁ θρόνος τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἀρνίου ἐν αὐτῇ ἔσται, καὶ οἱ δοῦλοι αὐτοῦ λατρεύσουσιν αὐτῷ,
verses.translit: kai pan katathema ouk estai eti. kai o thronos tou theou kai tou arnioy en aute estai, kai oi douloi autou latreysoysin auto,
verses.translation: And there shall be no more curse: but the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it; and his servants shall serve him:

verses.original: καὶ ὄψονται τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai opsontai to prosopon autou, kai to onoma autou epi ton metopon auton.
verses.translation: And they shall see his face; and his name shall be in their foreheads.

verses.original: καὶ νὺξ οὐκ ἔσται ⸀ἔτι, καὶ ⸂οὐκ ἔχουσιν χρείαν⸃ ⸀φωτὸς λύχνου καὶ ⸀φῶς ἡλίου, ὅτι κύριος ὁ θεὸς φωτίσει ⸀ἐπʼ αὐτούς, καὶ βασιλεύσουσιν εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων.
verses.translit: kai nux ouk estai eti, kai ouk ehoysin hreian fotos lyhnoy kai fos elioy, oti kyrios o theos fotisei ep' autoys, kai vasileysoysin eis tous aionas ton aionon.
verses.translation: And there shall be no night there; and they need no candle, neither light of the sun; for the Lord God giveth them light: and they shall reign for ever and ever.

verses.original: Καὶ ⸀εἶπέν μοι· Οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι πιστοὶ καὶ ἀληθινοί, καὶ ⸀ὁ κύριος, ὁ θεὸς τῶν πνευμάτων τῶν προφητῶν, ἀπέστειλεν τὸν ἄγγελον αὐτοῦ δεῖξαι τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ ἃ δεῖ γενέσθαι ἐν τάχει·
verses.translit: Kai eipen moi* Outoi oi logoi pistoi kai alithinoi, kai o kyrios, o theos ton pneymaton ton profiton, apesteilen ton aggelon autou deixai tois doylois autou a dei genesthai en tahei*
verses.translation: And he said unto me, These sayings are faithful and true: and the Lord God of the holy prophets sent his angel to shew unto his servants the things which must shortly be done.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἔρχομαι ταχύ· μακάριος ὁ τηρῶν τοὺς λόγους τῆς προφητείας τοῦ βιβλίου τούτου.
verses.translit: kai idou erhomai tahy* makarios o tiron tous logoys tes profiteias tou vivlioy toytoy.
verses.translation: Behold, I come quickly: blessed is he that keepeth the sayings of the prophecy of this book.

verses.original: Κἀγὼ Ἰωάννης ὁ ἀκούων καὶ βλέπων ταῦτα. καὶ ὅτε ἤκουσα καὶ ἔβλεψα, ἔπεσα προσκυνῆσαι ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ποδῶν τοῦ ἀγγέλου τοῦ δεικνύοντός μοι ταῦτα.
verses.translit: Kago Ioannis o akoyon kai vlepon tauta. kai ote ekoysa kai evlepsa, epesa proskynesai emprosthen ton podon tou aggeloy tou deiknyontos moi tauta.
verses.translation: And I John saw these things, and heard them . And when I had heard and seen, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel which shewed me these things.

verses.original: καὶ λέγει μοι· Ὅρα μή· σύνδουλός σού εἰμι καὶ τῶν ἀδελφῶν σου τῶν προφητῶν καὶ τῶν τηρούντων τοὺς λόγους τοῦ βιβλίου τούτου· τῷ θεῷ προσκύνησον.
verses.translit: kai legei moi* Ora mi* syndoylos soy eimi kai ton adelfon soy ton profiton kai ton tiroynton tous logoys tou vivlioy toytoy* to theo proskynison.
verses.translation: Then saith he unto me, See thou do it not: for I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets, and of them which keep the sayings of this book: worship God.

verses.original: Καὶ λέγει μοι· Μὴ σφραγίσῃς τοὺς λόγους τῆς προφητείας τοῦ βιβλίου τούτου, ὁ καιρὸς γὰρ ἐγγύς ἐστιν.
verses.translit: Kai legei moi* Me sfragises tous logoys tes profiteias tou vivlioy toytoy, o kairos gar eggys estin.
verses.translation: And he saith unto me, Seal not the sayings of the prophecy of this book: for the time is at hand.

verses.original: ὁ ἀδικῶν ἀδικησάτω ἔτι, καὶ ὁ ῥυπαρὸς ⸀ῥυπαρευθήτω ἔτι, καὶ ὁ δίκαιος δικαιοσύνην ποιησάτω ἔτι, καὶ ὁ ἅγιος ἁγιασθήτω ἔτι.
verses.translit: o adikon adikisato eti, kai o Ryparos Rypareythito eti, kai o dikaios dikaiosynin poiisato eti, kai o agios agiasthito eti.
verses.translation: He that is unjust, let him be unjust still: and he which is filthy, let him be filthy still: and he that is righteous, let him be righteous still: and he that is holy, let him be holy still.

verses.original: Ἰδοὺ ἔρχομαι ταχύ, καὶ ὁ μισθός μου μετʼ ἐμοῦ, ἀποδοῦναι ἑκάστῳ ὡς τὸ ἔργον ⸀ἐστὶν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Idou erhomai tahy, kai o misthos moy met' emou, apodounai ekasto os to ergon estin autou.
verses.translation: And, behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be.

verses.original: ἐγὼ τὸ Ἄλφα καὶ τὸ Ὦ, ὁ πρῶτος καὶ ὁ ἔσχατος, ⸀ἡ ἀρχὴ καὶ ⸀τὸ τέλος.
verses.translit: ego to Alfa kai to O, o protos kai o eshatos, e arhe kai to telos.
verses.translation: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last.

verses.original: Μακάριοι οἱ ⸂πλύνοντες τὰς στολὰς αὐτῶν⸃, ἵνα ἔσται ἡ ἐξουσία αὐτῶν ἐπὶ τὸ ξύλον τῆς ζωῆς καὶ τοῖς πυλῶσιν εἰσέλθωσιν εἰς τὴν πόλιν.
verses.translit: Makarioi oi plynontes tas stolas auton, ina estai e exoysia auton epi to xylon tes zoes kai tois pylosin eiselthosin eis ten polin.
verses.translation: Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.

verses.original: ἔξω οἱ κύνες καὶ οἱ φάρμακοι καὶ οἱ πόρνοι καὶ οἱ φονεῖς καὶ οἱ εἰδωλολάτραι καὶ πᾶς φιλῶν καὶ ποιῶν ψεῦδος.
verses.translit: exo oi kynes kai oi farmakoi kai oi pornoi kai oi foneis kai oi eidololatrai kai pas filon kai poion pseudos.
verses.translation: For without are dogs, and sorcerers, and whoremongers, and murderers, and idolaters, and whosoever loveth and maketh a lie.

verses.original: Ἐγὼ Ἰησοῦς ἔπεμψα τὸν ἄγγελόν μου μαρτυρῆσαι ὑμῖν ταῦτα ἐπὶ ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις. ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ῥίζα καὶ τὸ γένος Δαυίδ, ὁ ἀστὴρ ὁ λαμπρός, ὁ πρωϊνός.
verses.translit: Ego Iisous epempsa ton aggelon moy martyresai umin tauta epi tais ekklisiais. ego eimi e Riza kai to genos Dayid, o aster o lampros, o proinos.
verses.translation: I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.

verses.original: καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα καὶ ἡ νύμφη λέγουσιν· Ἔρχου· καὶ ὁ ἀκούων εἰπάτω· Ἔρχου· καὶ ὁ διψῶν ἐρχέσθω, ὁ θέλων λαβέτω ὕδωρ ζωῆς δωρεάν.
verses.translit: kai to pneuma kai e nymfi legoysin* Erhoy* kai o akoyon eipato* Erhoy* kai o dipson erhestho, o thelon laveto udor zoes dorean.
verses.translation: And the Spirit and the bride say, Come. And let him that heareth say, Come. And let him that is athirst come. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely.

verses.original: Μαρτυρῶ ἐγὼ παντὶ τῷ ἀκούοντι τοὺς λόγους τῆς προφητείας τοῦ βιβλίου τούτου· ἐάν τις ἐπιθῇ ἐπʼ αὐτά, ⸀ἐπιθήσει ὁ θεὸς ἐπʼ αὐτὸν τὰς πληγὰς τὰς γεγραμμένας ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τούτῳ·
verses.translit: Martyro ego panti to akoyonti tous logoys tes profiteias tou vivlioy toytoy* ean tis epithe ep' auta, epithisei o theos ep' auton tas pligas tas gegrammenas en to vivlio toyto*
verses.translation: For I testify unto every man that heareth the words of the prophecy of this book, If any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book:

verses.original: καὶ ἐάν τις ἀφέλῃ ἀπὸ τῶν λόγων τοῦ βιβλίου τῆς προφητείας ταύτης, ⸀ἀφελεῖ ὁ θεὸς τὸ μέρος αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου τῆς ζωῆς καὶ ἐκ τῆς πόλεως τῆς ἁγίας, τῶν γεγραμμένων ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τούτῳ.
verses.translit: kai ean tis afele apo ton logon tou vivlioy tes profiteias taytis, afelei o theos to meros autou apo tou xyloy tes zoes kai ek tes poleos tes agias, ton gegrammenon en to vivlio toyto.
verses.translation: And if any man shall take away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his part out of the book of life, and out of the holy city, and from the things which are written in this book.

verses.original: Λέγει ὁ μαρτυρῶν ταῦτα· Ναί· ἔρχομαι ταχύ. Ἀμήν· ⸀ἔρχου, κύριε Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: Legei o martyron tauta* Nai* erhomai tahy. Amin* erhoy, kyrie Iisou.
verses.translation: He which testifieth these things saith, Surely I come quickly. Amen. Even so, come, Lord Jesus.

verses.original: Ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου ⸀Ἰησοῦ μετὰ ⸀πάντων.
verses.translit: E haris tou kyrioy Iisou meta panton.
verses.translation: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
